feat(features): add legacy-compatible response

Add buildLegacyCompatibleFeaturesResponse to adapt the new features/capabilities payload into a shape expected by older mobile clients. Update /v1/features route to return the legacy-compatible payload and add an integration test (with a Zod schema) that verifies mapping for bugReports, voice, social.friends, oauth providers, auth recovery, and automations.existingSessionTarget. fix(features): hide retention when disabled

Add a guard to omit retention capabilities when retention is not effectively enabled by calling resolveEffectiveRetentionEnabled in serverRetentionCapabilitiesFeature. Return an empty delta if retention is disabled to avoid exposing retention capabilities. Also add an integration test to verify capabilities.server.retention is undefined when retention env flags indicate disabled state.

feat(pipeline): add --runtime-version for OTA

Add a --runtime-version CLI flag and HAPPIER_EXPO_RUNTIME_VERSION env override to OTA flows. run.mjs accepts and forwards --runtime-version to delegated expo OTA commands (and validates it is only used with --action ota). ota-update.mjs injects HAPPIER_EXPO_RUNTIME_VERSION into the environment when provided. apps/ui/app.config.js will prefer the explicit HAPPIER_EXPO_RUNTIME_VERSION over the runtimeVersion policy. Tests and contract tests were added/updated to cover forwarding and env propagation. This enables creating maintenance OTA updates that target a specific older runtime version.

fix(sync): expand fallback errors for session RPC

Treat additional RPC/socket failures as safe to fallback to the socket commit path. Add readRpcErrorCode usage to detect RPC_ERROR_CODES.METHOD_NOT_FOUND, and check error messages for 'Method not found', 'Socket connect timeout' and any 'connect_error' occurrences. Update tests to parametrize these failure cases via createFallbackSafeSessionRpcErrors and it.each to ensure sendMessage falls back correctly. This improves compatibility with older daemons/preview CLIs and handles reconnect churn.

fix(popover): avoid redundant geometry re-renders

Prevent unnecessary Popover re-renders when computed layout or render props don't meaningfully change. Introduce RECT_UPDATE_TOLERANCE (1px) and helper equality checks (arePopoverRenderPropsEqual, areWindowRectsEqual), and guard state updates to reuse previous state when values are effectively equal. Add a native keyboard test to ensure a keyboard-triggered recompute that results in the same geometry does not cause an extra render.

fix(sessions): disable native inline drag on Android (hot patch)

Temporarily disable native inline drag on Android as a hotfix and ensure long-press context menu behaviour remains correct on iOS. Changes:

- SessionsList: stop wrapping rows in a GestureDetector, always pass reorder gesture to SessionItem, enable nativeInlineDrag only on iOS, and disable drag activation/onLongPress on Android.
- useSessionInlineDrag: add an optional `enabled` param, return no gesture and a neutral animatedStyle when disabled, and include `enabled` in deps.
- SessionItem: only enable long-press context menu on iOS (or when a reorder handle is shown) to avoid conflicts on Android.
- Tests: update and add tests to cover iOS vs Android behaviour, ensure gestures are not provided when disabled, and mock Platform.OS dynamically in tests.

This change avoids Android-specific gesture/context-menu conflicts while preserving iOS reorder UX; it's implemented as a targeted platform check/hotfix and accompanied by unit test updates.

feat(claude): normalize CLI session-control modes

Add normalizeClaudeHappyCliSessionControlPermissionMode to canonicalize session-control flags passed through the Happier CLI before launching Claude. This maps Happier-accepted tokens to Claude-compatible names (yolo → bypassPermissions, safe-yolo → acceptEdits) while leaving other modes unchanged; notably, read-only is not rewritten to dontAsk at this boundary.

feat(spawn): support legacy daemon spawn payloads

Add compatibility handling for older daemon CLI versions when spawning sessions and using session runtime RPCs. Introduces legacy spawn payload types and builders (LegacySpawnHappySessionRpcParams, buildLegacySpawnHappySessionRpcParams) and a compatibility entrypoint (buildCompatibleSpawnHappySessionRpcParams) along with a version gate (shouldUseLegacySpawnHappySessionRpcParams).

Enhance version utilities to normalize dev/preview suffixes and add MINIMUM_CLI_BACKEND_TARGET_SPAWN_VERSION and MINIMUM_CLI_SESSION_USER_MESSAGE_RPC_VERSION constants so dev builds (e.g. 0.1.0-dev.x) are correctly treated as compatible. machineSpawnNewSession now reads the machine's CLI version and either returns an informative error for unsupported daemon versions or selects the legacy/modern payload accordingly. Also gate session user-message runtime RPC usage in sync based on session CLI version.

Small CLI change: normalize Claude-compatible permission modes for daemon session spawn args. Add and update tests to cover legacy payload construction, dev-version handling, RPC gating, and permission-mode normalization.
Add funding configuration for GitHub and custom links

fix(sync): normalize socket path and withCredentials

Normalize socket endpoints to strip trailing slashes and use the canonical '/v1/updates/' path, and explicitly disable credentialed polling (withCredentials: false). This prevents xhr poll errors caused by mismatched Engine.IO endpoints and blocked credentialed cross-origin polling; the server authenticates via the handshake token and CORS is configured without credentials. Also ensure provided transports are not overridden in web runtimes. Updated/added tests and adjusted socket creation in createSyncSocketTransport, createConcurrentServerSocketTransport, and serverScopedRpcSocketPool to reflect these behaviors.

fix(sync): remap legacy directory error

Remap misleading legacy daemon errors when the server returns INVALID_REQUEST with message "Directory is required" even though the app sent a directory. Add remapLegacyDirectoryCompatibilityError and apply it to normalized spawn-session results in machineSpawnNewSession to surface a clearer compatibility hint (suggesting restart/re-authorize and updating to a compatible daemon). Also add a unit test to verify the mapped error for a legacy machine entry.

feat(sessions): add HTTP compat for legacy session routes

Add a compatibility layer to handle older session HTTP responses and missing /v2 endpoints. Introduce sessionHttpCompat.ts which parses/coerces legacy session rows, detects missing /v2 session routes, and falls back to scanning /v1 session lists. Integrate these fallbacks into fetchAndApplySessionById and fetchAndApplySessions so single-session and snapshot fetches accept legacy payload shapes and gracefully handle 404s or invalid /v2 responses. Update tests to cover legacy payload handling and the /v1 fallback paths.

feat(sessions): reconcile persisted machine/path

Add support for applying persisted draft machine and path to the new-session selection state. The hook now accepts persistedMachineId and persistedPath, resolves persisted IDs to current machines, and prefers persisted paths when initializing or reconciling selection (while respecting explicit route params and user actions). Implements reconciliation logic to swap an offline persisted machine to a matching online machine, avoids reapplying persisted values after user selection, and tracks the last-applied persisted machine to prevent duplicate work. Wire persistedDraft/hydratedPersistedAuthoringDraft into useNewSessionScreenModel and update tests/mocks (including a new test for reconciling offline persisted machines and other expectations around draft hydration).

fix(sessions): handle v2 by-id 404 and strict compat parsing

Distinguish current-server /v2/sessions/:id 404 payloads from missing-route 404s and avoid unnecessary compat scanning by returning { ok: false, session: null, errorCode: 'not_found', httpStatus: 404 } when the v2-by-id not-found schema matches. Add looksLikeCurrentV2SessionNotFound404 and wire it into fetchAndApplySessionById, plus tests for the 404 contract.

Also tighten compatibility parsing for /v2/sessions list pages: treat any malformed row as a fatal parse error (reject pages that mix valid and malformed rows) and add a test that snapshot loading fails when a compat page contains both valid and invalid rows. Files changed: sessionById.ts, sessionHttpCompat.ts, sessionById.test.ts, syncSessions.v2SessionsFetch.test.ts.

fix(tools): fallback to tool.id for permission id

Add resolvePermissionRequestId helper and use it across AcpHistoryImportView, AskUserQuestionView, and ExitPlanToolView to fallback to tool.id when permission metadata is missing (e.g. during reconnect recovery). Also treat tools with no permission but state === 'running' as pending in AcpHistoryImportView. Update tests to cover reconnect scenarios and ensure approve/reject/answer flows use the fallback id when permission.id is not yet reattached.

refactor(sessions): remove CLI banner logic

Remove CliNotDetectedBanner usage and related props from NewSessionWizard and its hook helpers. The import and rendering of per-agent CLI banners were removed, along with the isCliBannerDismissed and dismissCliBanner props and the CliNotDetectedBannerDismissScope type usage in useNewSessionScreenModel and useNewSessionWizardProps. Tests were updated to mock the banner and add assertions ensuring CLI banners are not rendered in the AI backend section and that AI backend providers render correctly. This reduces the prop surface and centralizes CLI-detection/banner handling elsewhere.

fix(fs): add cross-device rename fallback

Handle EXDEV errors when renaming files by adding moveFileWithCrossDeviceFallback and using it in finalizeWorkspaceFileUpload. The new helper attempts a normal rename, falls back to copying to a staged temp file in the destination directory and renaming that, then removes the source; it also cleans up the staged temp on errors. Added a test (finalizeWorkspaceFileUpload.test.ts) that simulates a cross-device rename error to verify the fallback and cleanup behavior.

refactor(agent): drop composer user-action cards

Stop rendering user-action prompt cards in the composer permission chrome and simplify permission request handling. Remove composerUserActionRequests usage and resolveAgentRequestKind import from AgentInput; only permission requests are considered when computing permission locations and rendering AgentInputPermissionRequests. AgentInputPermissionRequests now treats userActionRequests as optional and renders only PermissionPromptCard entries. Tests updated to expect no user-action cards in the composer surface.

fix(claude): canonicalize Claude entrypoint paths

Resolve PATH and install entrypoints to their real on-disk locations before returning them. Add canonicalizeClaudeEntrypointPath (uses realpathSync with fallback) and use it in getDefaultClaudeCodePathForAgentSdk; update tests to expect realpathSync results and add a symlink canonicalization test. This prevents returning symlink paths (or inconsistent PATH entries) and ensures the Agent SDK receives a real, executable entrypoint.

feat(sessions): add maxBytes option to sessionReadFile

Add an optional maxBytes option to sessionReadFile so callers can request a larger inline read limit (useful for image previews). resolveSessionFileInlineMaxBytes was refactored to accept a defaultMaxBytes so callers can supply an override while still respecting the hard cap. The image preview hook now passes a maxPreviewBytes override, and sessionWriteFile call sites explicitly pass the default constant. Tests updated to assert that a larger preview-sized inline read succeeds when maxBytes is provided. Default behavior and hard limits remain unchanged.

fix(ui): reserve extra room for accessory icons

Increase reserved width for accessory/selection icons and ensure icon-like components keep their element shape and size across platforms.

- Bumped icon slot widths from 24 to 28 in ProfilesList, PathSelector, SearchableListSelector and NewSessionWizard to provide extra spacing for selection indicators.
- Align iOS comfortable density to 32 (ITEM_ICON_BOX_SIZE) to match the new reserved space.
- Add resizeAccessoryIconForDensity and apply it to Item left/accessory nodes so icon-like accessories are resized to the resolved density box size instead of being embedded or left unscaled.
- Update normalizeNodeForView to detect icon-like elements and only wrap them in Text on web (avoid wrapping on native), preventing icons from being converted to text nodes on iOS.
- Add and update tests for ProfilesList, PathSelector, Item subtitle normalization, item density metrics and normalizeNodeForView to cover spacing, sizing and wrapping behavior.

These changes fix visual/spacing regressions and ensure consistent icon density and rendering behavior across web and native platforms.

fix(sessions): apply top safe-area to wizard

Forward safeAreaTop and newSessionTopPadding through the wizard props and use safeAreaTop to set paddingTop on the wizard content wrapper so the UI respects iOS top insets. Add default values in NewSessionWizard, update useNewSessionWizardProps and useNewSessionScreenModel to pass the new params, and extend the test to assert the top inset is applied and related layout expectations (including codex row width). This prevents the wizard content from being overlapped by the iOS safe area.

feat(system-status): display app runtime info

Add runtime metadata to the System Status screen and a helper to read it from Expo modules.

- Add readCurrentAppRuntimeInfo util (expo-application, expo-constants, expo-updates) to surface appVersion, native versions, applicationId, update channel/id/runtime/createdAt and launch source
- Integrate util into SystemStatusView, expose application section with items for native/OTA details and include updates object in the captured environment payload
- Add unit tests for readCurrentAppRuntimeInfo
- Add translations for the new "application" section and labels across multiple locales

This makes native and OTA diagnostics visible in the settings UI to aid debugging and telemetry.

feat(auth): add shared scanned auth URL processor

Introduce a unified handler for scanned authentication URLs and custom scheme parsing.

- Add useScannedAuthUrlProcessor hook to route scanned URLs to account or terminal flows and surface a single processAuthUrl API.
- Add ScanAuthQrScreen component that reuses QrCodeScannerView and the new processor; replace ScanAccount and ScanTerminal screens to use this shared component.
- Add parseHappierCustomSchemeUrl utility and update pairing/account/terminal deep-link parsers to accept alternate custom-scheme forms (e.g. "happier:account?...").
- Update SettingsView to route manually entered auth URLs through the shared processor.
- Update QrCodeScannerView to account for safe-area insets when laying out overlay controls while keeping the camera full-bleed.
- Update and add tests across scanners, parsers, settings, and QR scanner behaviour to reflect the new routing and parsing logic.

These changes centralize URL processing, support more custom URI variations, and reduce duplication across account/terminal scanning flows.

feat(process): prefer PATHEXT .cmd shims

Normalize Windows command resolution to prefer PATHEXT-resolved .cmd/.bat shims over extensionless files.

Adds resolveWindowsCommandPath and buildWindowsCommandCandidates helpers and exports them from the cli-common process module. resolveWindowsCommandOnPath and resolveWindowsCommandInvocation now use a unified candidate list so explicit paths without extensions are normalized to their matching .cmd shim when present. Several consumer modules (provider resolution, managed JS runtime, codex backend, agent override) were updated to normalize Windows override paths before performing access checks. Tests and pipeline scripts were added/updated to cover the new Windows behavior.

This ensures Windows behavior matches PATHEXT semantics and avoids running extensionless files when a shell shim is available.

feat(agents): support reasoningEffort overrides

Add support for adopting reasoningEffort overrides from message metadata and propagate optimistic ACP config-option overrides into next message meta.

- AgentInput UI: adjust single-pane detailed layout and add related tests.

These changes ensure per-message reasoning effort can be set by clients and that optimistic config changes are reflected in outgoing messages and UI.

feat(pipeline): add expo-testflight-distribute

Add a new pipeline subcommand to distribute iOS TestFlight builds to external groups via the App Store Connect API.

This change adds the main distribution script and several helpers plus tests and CI wiring:
- scripts/pipeline/expo/testflight-distribute.mjs: new CLI script that resolves an EAS build, waits for ASC processing, attaches builds to external TestFlight groups, and submits Beta App Review.
- scripts/pipeline/expo/*.mjs: supporting helpers (asc builds URL, EAS CLI args, group resolution) and unit tests.
- scripts/pipeline/run.mjs: integrate the new subcommand and add a helper to execute the script.
- scripts/pipeline/cli/help-specs/expo.mjs: add help/usage for expo-testflight-distribute.
- .github/workflows/publish-ui-mobile-dev.yml: optional workflow step to run distribution when APP_STORE_CONNECT_PUBLICDEV_EXTERNAL_GROUPS is configured.

fix(cli-claude): resolve npm global claude install via process.execPath

The Agent SDK path resolver could not find Claude Code when it was
installed via an npm global prefix whose `node` directory was not
reliably present on PATH at runtime. This happens in two common setups:

- Windows + nvm-windows, where `C:\Program Files\nodejs` is a junction
  to the active version and may be missing from a daemon-spawned child
  process's PATH.
- Detached daemons on any platform whose PATH has been stripped down
  to a service-default set that does not include the npm global prefix
  (the same class of issue addressed by #42 for systemd on Linux).

In those environments every existing fallback (`resolveProviderCliCommand`,
the versioned installer dir, the native installer locations) fails, and
users see the confusing "Claude Code is not installed (or not detectable)"
error even though `claude` works fine from their interactive shell.

This change adds a new fallback step that derives the npm global
`@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js` entrypoint directly from
`process.execPath`, which always points to the active `node` binary
regardless of PATH state. Both the Windows layout
(`<execDir>/node_modules/...`) and the Unix layout
(`<execDir>/../lib/node_modules/...`) are checked.

Includes unit tests that stub `process.execPath` to a sandbox directory
and verify the new resolution path on both platform shapes. The existing
tests are also updated to isolate `process.execPath` so the host's real
npm global install cannot bleed into the assertions.

fix(cli-claude): address review feedback on npm global resolution

Addresses three review findings on #153:

- CodeRabbit (Major): drop canonicalizeClaudeEntrypointPath() on the
  npm-global fallback path. Canonicalization resolves symlinks and
  junctions (including nvm-windows C:\Program Files\nodejs) to their
  version-pinned targets, which breaks the "preserve symlinks so Claude
  auto-updates can retarget the same path" pattern that the PATH
  resolution branch already follows.

- Greptile (P2): move the npm-global step to run AFTER the Unix
  versioned-install probe, so a user with both a newer
  ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ install and an older npm-global
  install still gets the versioned one.

- Greptile (P2): strengthen the inline comment on the candidate array
  in findClaudeInNpmGlobalModules() to explicitly explain why checking
  the Windows candidate first is safe on Unix (that path layout never
  exists there).

Tests: 15/15 passing. No behavior change in the PATH happy path or in
the HAPPIER_CLAUDE_PATH override branch.

These changes make installer output more discoverable and help users complete follow-up steps after installation.

feat(cli-common): resolve tsc via package manager

Use the active package-manager path (npm_execpath) and candidate commands to invoke tsc instead of hardcoding a repo-root TypeScript binary. - Add a unit test to verify Windows yarn.cmd fallback when spawning fails (verifyExports.test.mjs).

feat(cli): prefer Windows packaged binary to speedup session startup on Windows

Add an opt-in launch option to prefer using a sibling packaged Windows executable when spawning CLI subprocesses on Windows. Introduces a new HappyCliSubprocessLaunchOptions { preferWindowsPackagedBinary } and a 'binary' runtime path that resolves a sibling happier.exe next to package-dist entrypoints; buildHappyCliSubprocessInvocation/launchSpec and spawnHappyCLI were updated to accept and propagate the option. startDaemon now requests this preference for daemon-launched sessions; tests were added/updated to cover execPath behavior and integration wiring. The behavior is gated by platform and the HAPPIER_WINDOWS_SESSION_RUNNER_BINARY env var (can be used to disable). Files changed: startDaemon, spawnHappyCLI, tests, and testkit env keys.

refactor(scripts): centralize yarn/command spawning

Introduce a unified runCommand helper and use resolveYarnCommandInvocation across scripts and tests to normalize how yarn (and other commands) are spawned, especially on Windows. Replaces ad-hoc spawn logic with runCommand in server scripts, updates many test and tooling scripts to call resolveYarnCommandInvocation and pass through windowsVerbatimArguments when needed, and adapts test expectations to ensure the Windows yarn shim is invoked via cmd.exe and does not include npm_cli shims. This unifies behavior around npm_execpath handling and reduces duplicate spawn/argument handling code.

fix(scripts): resolve Yarn invocations on Windows

Implement resolveServerScriptCommandInvocation to robustly resolve server script commands (especially Yarn) across platforms. Distinguish npm_execpath values (avoiding npm-cli.js being treated as Yarn), support nested Yarn via node-runner when npm_execpath points to a Yarn CLI, and build a cmd.exe shim with proper escaping and windowsVerbatimArguments for .cmd/.bat invocations on Windows. Update runCommand to use the new resolver and add unit tests (runCommand.spec.ts) to cover loading from a partial repo copy and Windows/Linux Yarn resolution scenarios.

feat(sessions): use start-side ellipsis for web path

Add web-specific handling for path subtitles to preserve path order while showing a start-side overflow ellipsis.

- SessionItem.tsx: add styles sessionPathSubtitleWeb and sessionPathSubtitleTextWeb and apply them when rendering path subtitles on web. Wrap the subtitle text in an inner LTR Text while the outer container uses RTL to emulate head-ellipsis on web; use native 'head' ellipsizeMode for non-web platforms.
- SessionItem.activityTime.test.tsx: add tests for web vs native path subtitle ellipsing, introduce a platformOs test variable and Platform mock select/getter, and add a flattenStyle helper to inspect composed styles in the tests.

This ensures long path subtitles on the web show a start-side ellipsis without reordering path segments, while preserving native behavior on mobile.

fix(ui): exit on session delete and invalid route

feat(session): propagate archivedAt to clients

Include archivedAt in update-session payloads and event types, and emit update events when sessions are archived/unarchived so participants receive the change. Filter archived sessions out of the regular paged listing and add support for fetching the archived snapshot via a /v2/sessions/archived path. Make socket handling and sync apply cache-only session-list renderable patches (archived/active state and activity patches) so UI can update cached rows without forcing full hydration. Add UI improvements: archived screen fetch-on-mount, show cached archived rows before hydration, and session item skeleton title while metadata is pending. Update and add tests and mocks across server and client to cover these behaviors.

fix(cli): remove hidden change-title instruction

Stop automatically appending the hidden change-title instruction to user prompts across backends and update related tests. Remove change-title injection logic from Claude SDK backend and remote launcher, and from the OpenCode runtime; update tests to assert prompts are sent verbatim. Add PATCH sessionUpdate support to the OpenCode client and ensure the runtime updates session permissions before continuing/resuming prompts. Improve resumed-session handling by tracking vendor-assigned user message IDs and effective prompt text to avoid streaming vendor-assigned resumed user snapshots as assistant output. Misc: tweak tests and types to reflect these behavioral changes.

feat(sessions): wait for stop exit and retry archive

Add coordinated wait-for-exit and improved archive retry behavior for sessions.

- CLI/daemon: introduce HAPPIER_DAEMON_STOP_SESSION_WAIT_FOR_EXIT_MS (default 15000) and HAPPIER_DAEMON_STOP_SESSION_WAIT_FOR_EXIT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS (default 100) in configuration. startDaemon now defaults HAPPIER_DAEMON_SESSION_RESPAWN_ENABLED to false, marks stops on the respawn manager, and stopSession will wait (when enabled) for the tracked runner to be observed exited before returning, calling onChildExited for observed PIDs.
- Sessions helper: waitForExistingSessionExitIfStopRequested now collects matching PIDs and accepts an onExitObserved callback that is invoked when a previously stop-requested tracked runner is no longer active.
- UI: session archive flow now treats repeated server-side "session_active" responses as transient and retries until a timeout; increased default retry delay to 200ms and replace max-retries with a timeout env EXPO_PUBLIC_HAPPIER_SESSION_ARCHIVE_AFTER_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS (default 75000ms). Export isSessionActiveArchiveResult and use it to trigger stop-then-archive flows when appropriate.
- SessionItem and related components: change swipe action to always perform archive (stop then archive for active sessions), add identity skeleton UI while metadata loads, and wire stop-then-archive retry behavior into multiple UI flows.
- server-scoped ops/tests: prefer daemon machine RPC for stopping sessions when the hosting machine is reachable and fall back to session RPCs; tests and mocks updated to reflect storage state and machine RPC usage.

Multiple tests and integration tests added/updated to cover the new waiting, retrying and RPC-fallback behaviors.

fix: retry metadata/agent-state writes on transient network failure

updateMetadataBestEffort and updateAgentStateBestEffort previously made
a single fire-and-forget attempt. On flaky or mobile connections a
transient error would silently swallow the write, leaving the session
without a persisted vendorResumeId (e.g. claudeSessionId) and making
the session permanently non-resumable.

Change both helpers to retry up to 3 times (immediate → +1 s → +2 s)
before giving up. Failures on intermediate attempts are logged at debug
level; only the final failure is flagged. Behaviour on success is
unchanged.

fix: address PR review — unref timer, add docstrings, couple delay/attempts

- Derive BEST_EFFORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS from BEST_EFFORT_RETRY_DELAYS_MS.length + 1
  so the two constants can't silently drift out of sync
- unref() the retry timer so pending best-effort retries never hold the Node
  process open past daemon shutdown
- Add JSDoc to withRetry, updateAgentStateBestEffort, updateMetadataBestEffort
  to satisfy docstring coverage requirement; document intentional retry-all
  behaviour
fix(cli): persist session metadata writes reliably

fix: add @fastify/compress to reduce bundle transfer size on mobile

The server was serving the web UI JS bundle (~19MB) uncompressed. On
mobile networks this caused connections to drop mid-transfer, resulting
in the iOS app showing "Server not supported — unexpected response".

Registers @fastify/compress globally so all responses (including the
static JS bundle) are compressed with gzip/zstd. This fixes the issue
at the server layer for all self-hosted deployments, regardless of
whether they use Caddy, nginx, or any other proxy.

fix(server): actively checkpoint sqlite WAL to prevent checkpoint starvation

On the light/sqlite flavor the WAL could be starved by long-lived overlapping
readers: passive autocheckpoint never reset it, so the WAL grew without bound,
reads slowed as they scanned WAL frames, and writes eventually exceeded Prisma's
query timeout and surfaced as `Socket timeout` errors. The server then appeared
"crashed" (sessions offline) while CPU sat idle, and only a manual restart +
`wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` recovered it.

Add an actively-driven WAL checkpoint worker that runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`
on an interval (configurable via HAPPIER_SQLITE_WAL_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_MS, default
60s, 0 disables) for sqlite, stopped on shutdown. Also apply `PRAGMA journal_size_limit`
(default 64MiB, configurable) as a retained-WAL safety net, surfaced in startup
diagnostics. Bounds the WAL regardless of reader pressure.

Fixes #189

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(server): address review feedback on sqlite WAL checkpoint worker

- Clamp the checkpoint interval to setInterval's 32-bit max (a larger value is
  silently coerced to 1ms, turning the worker into a hot loop); reject out-of-range
  values in the resolver.
- Read the wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) result by SQLite's documented column names with
  a positional fallback, instead of relying solely on Object.values() order.
- Use the @/storage/prisma alias import per server conventions.
- Add resolver tests for non-safe-integer and beyond-32-bit-bound inputs.

Keep the CLI dist snapshot and workspace payload copy under the same lock generation, reclaim abandoned snapshots before creating a new one, and restore a previous dist if compilation fails. Release-runtime and transfers now emit their normal `dist` surfaces so packaged entrypoints remain stable.

* fix(protocol): fail-soft on malformed claude assistant transcript rows

RawAgentOutputDataUnknownSchema carried a refine() that rejected any
output `type` present in the known set. Combined with
union([Known, Unknown]), a known-type row whose body did not match its
known variant (e.g. a Claude `assistant` row missing `message`, with
`message.role` missing, or with `content: null`) failed BOTH branches,
so the whole record failed validation and the UI rendered
"[Unparsed agent message]".

Remove the refine so malformed known-type rows fall through to the
catch-all. union([Known, Unknown]) tries Known first, so well-formed
rows still get their rich Known variant (no behavior change for the
happy path). The branded .transform() is preserved so TS narrowing on
`data.type` keeps working.

This realizes the stated intent of commit 4dd41fcbc ("fail-soft
transcript normalization"), whose Unknown catch-all was meant to absorb
malformed records but was blocked by the collide-refine.

Add regression tests for the three real-world failing shapes plus a
no-regression test for well-formed rows. unparsed_message_error.md
documents the full root-cause analysis.

Transcript placeholder rows are diagnostics, not conversation content. Every user saw

maintainer can act on, while the payload type that makes them diagnosable is only useful with
developer tooling at hand.

`resolveUnsupportedContentPresentation` is the single owner of that decision:

- developer diagnostics on (dev build or the `devModeEnabled` local setting, via the existing
  `isSessionDebugInformationEnabled` owner): keep the raw fallback text, so the offending payload
  type stays greppable — the detail whose absence let a new Claude record type go unnoticed for a

- diagnostics off: agent-side placeholders render no row at all;
- a user's own unparsed message always keeps a labeled placeholder, because a gap where the user
  knows they typed something is a trust problem rather than noise.

Hiding happens in `MessageViewWithSessionCommon`, next to the existing voice-agent-turn guard, so
toggling the setting can never change the hook order of a mounted message block. Selection follows
the same owner: a row that is not rendered is not selectable and cannot be copied, and copying a

feat(protocol): add MiniMax built-in backend profiles (global + CN) (#212)

* feat(protocol): add MiniMax built-in backend profiles (global + CN)

Add global and China MiniMax built-in backend profiles using the
Anthropic-compatible and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Both profiles map
MiniMax-M3 as the default model and MiniMax-M2.7 as the small/fast model,
wire ANTHROPIC_* and OPENAI_* environment variables, and are compatible
with the Claude and Codex agents. Register the new profile ids in the UI
profile metadata, documentation, and translation strings.

* fix(protocol): scope MiniMax profiles to Claude and modern model aliases

Codex CLI resolves its provider from ~/.codex/config.toml, never from
environment variables. Verified against openai/codex at rust-v0.145.0
and HEAD: the only OpenAI-namespace variables read anywhere in the
workspace are OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_PROJECT and OPENAI_ORGANIZATION.
OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_MODEL do not exist as environment reads, and
the base-URL override is the config key `openai_base_url`. The MiniMax
profiles therefore could not have configured a Codex session, so they no
longer advertise agent:codex compatibility.

Dropping the OPENAI_* block also stops a Claude session from exporting
the MiniMax key as OPENAI_API_KEY into every tool subprocess it spawns.

ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL is deprecated upstream and only covers the
Haiku tier. Replace it with the ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}
aliases already used by the Z.AI profile so that switching model in a
MiniMax session resolves to a real MiniMax model instead of sending the
literal alias upstream.

Documentation now records the endpoints' disjoint key namespaces and the
200K context window the Anthropic-compatible endpoint advertises despite
M3 being natively 1M.

* test(cli-profiles): cover the shipped MiniMax profile env contract

Exercises the real registry entries through buildProfileEnvOverlay rather
than a hand-built fixture, so the assertions fail if the regional
defaults, template expansion, alias routing, secret gate, or agent
compatibility regress.

Verified RED against the previous profile definition: the alias-routing,
OpenAI-namespace and Codex-compatibility cases fail, the secret-gate
cases pass in both states because that invariant already held.

* fix(protocol): follow MiniMax's documented 1M-context Claude Code setup

MiniMax's Claude Code guide specifies the `[1m]` extended-context model id
together with CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=1000000:

    ANTHROPIC_MODEL:                "MiniMax-M3[1m]"
    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: "MiniMax-M3[1m]"
    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL:   "MiniMax-M3[1m]"
    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL:  "MiniMax-M3[1m]"
    CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW: "1000000"

The two settings are a pair. Plain `MiniMax-M3` resolves to the 200K the
endpoint advertises, so the previous defaults would have compacted at
roughly a sixth of the model's real window. This supersedes the earlier
claim that the compaction window is a no-op here: it is only inert when
the selected model does not carry the extended-context suffix.

The Haiku tier keeps the cheaper documented M2.7 rather than mapping every
tier to M3, since Haiku-class background work is what that tier is for.
Every value stays overridable through its MINIMAX_* / MINIMAX_CN_* key.

* fix(server-version): drop the stale store version floor from /v1/version

IOS_UP_TO_DATE and ANDROID_UP_TO_DATE were introduced upstream in 0d9f19b9a
when the app shipped on the 1.4.x line and were never updated. Happier ships
0.2.x, so every native client failed `semver.satisfies('0.2.10', '>=1.4.1')`
and received a permanent, unactionable upgrade-required response.

Store link is retained as an upgrade destination for iOS when a real minimum
triggers and no upgrade URL is configured.

* fix(server-version): fail closed when required enforcement has an unusable policy

resolveSessionSyncCompatibilityPolicy falls back to FALLBACK_REQUIREMENTS when
the configured policy cannot be read, and that fallback carries no client
minimums. The version endpoint read those minimums directly, so a malformed
MINIMUM_VERSIONS_JSON — for example a non-comparable "1.2" — silently answered
`current` to every client while socket and HTTP enforcement were rejecting the
same clients via decision.ts.

Removing the hardcoded store floor made this reachable: it previously masked the
fallback by returning upgrade-required for unrelated reasons.

The endpoint now mirrors decision.ts and refuses to answer when enforcement is
required and the policy is invalid. Observe-mode operators still get `current`,
matching the existing observe-policy-invalid outcome.

fix(server-presence): clear session active on explicit stop disconnect

An accepted stop kills the runner, but the resulting publisher disconnect
only recorded observer loss and left `active` set. Archive is gated on
`active === false`, so it returned 409 session-active for the full
10-minute presence fence while the client retry budget is 75s, making
archive-after-stop impossible to complete from the UI.

Record intent only when a runner accepts a stop, and treat the disconnect
that follows as the termination it is. A superseded fence still protects a
successor publisher, and a failed stop records nothing so an incidental
disconnect cannot end a live session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(server-presence): persist explicit-stop intent on the session row

The intent lived in a process-local Map inside `createSessionPublisherPresence`.
With `redisRegistry.enabled` the stop RPC and the runner's publisher socket can
be served by different instances, so the disconnect handler never saw the
intent and the fix degraded to the pre-existing behaviour: archive stays 409
`session-active` for the full 10-minute presence fence.

Move the intent to `Session.stopRequestedAt`. `markExplicitStopRequested`
writes the timestamp; `forgetDisconnectedPublisher` reads and clears it inside
the transaction it already opens, so the consume and the close commit together.
`closeBindingAtFence` is split into an in-transaction owner plus a wrapper so
the disconnect path reuses it without nesting a second transaction. The TTL is
unchanged in meaning and is now a comparison against the persisted timestamp,
which also retires the unbounded-map sweep.

The intent write is awaited in `rpcHandler` because it is now durable: the
publisher disconnect that reads it can arrive as soon as the runner begins
tearing down.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(server-presence): invalidate stop intent when a successor publisher registers

`stopRequestedAt` is keyed by session, not by publisher, so a stop that never
killed its runner stayed readable after a successor took the session over. The
successor's own incidental disconnect then consumed it and closed a session
whose runner never agreed to stop — its fence was current, so nothing else
rejected the close.

A registering publisher is a new binding, so clear the intent in the update
`registerOnce` already performs. No extra query, and the fence check keeps
covering the opposite direction (a predecessor's stale fence).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(server-rpc): run the stop lifecycle on forwards without an acknowledgement

`forwardTargetResponse` owns explicit-stop intent recording and machine-scoped
stop finalization, but all three forward sites invoked it only inside
`if (callback)`. Socket.IO permits a caller to emit without an acknowledgement,
and such a stop was forwarded to the runner and accepted while the server
recorded nothing — leaving the session `active` for the full presence fence.

Evaluate the forwarded response on every successful forward and call back only
when the caller supplied one. Note that `callback?.(await forward(...))` does
not fix this: optional-call short-circuiting skips argument evaluation, so the
lifecycle never runs. The result is bound to a local first.

Not reachable from first-party clients today — every stop path uses
`emitWithAck` — so this closes the contract rather than an observed incident.

refactor(claude-models): give the Claude model list a single owner

Claude built its model list twice: the new-session preflight probe adapter and
the in-session sessionModelsV1 publisher, which rebuilt it from
AGENT_MODEL_CONFIG. Two producers of the same concept can disagree about which
models exist and which effort tiers they support.

Introduce one owner (backends/claude/models/resolveClaudeModelCatalog): the
curated catalog augmented with whatever the Anthropic Models API reports. Both
producers read it. Curated entries keep their hand-authored labels and effort
defaults, dated snapshot ids collapse onto their static alias, and models from a
generation below the curated floor are dropped — the Models API lists everything
the account may call, including generations Claude Code can no longer run. Any
failure falls back to the curated catalog. Results are cached per resolved
account config dir + endpoint + ambient-credential fingerprint, so a session
start does not pay a network round trip and a credential swap is not served a
previous account's list.

Credentials belong to the endpoint they are sent to. The catalog honors
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, because Happier's built-in Z.AI, DeepSeek, and MiniMax
Claude profiles point it at a gateway and pair it with a gateway-issued
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; the on-disk Claude Code subscription token is
Anthropic-only and is never sent to a third-party gateway. Credential precedence
mirrors isolateClaudeRuntimeAuthEnv: for a bound session the ambient auth env
keys the spawn would strip are ignored, keeping only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the
anthropic service. Reading a key the spawn deletes would describe one account for
a session that runs as another. The probe adapter is typed as a session controls
probe adapter — the shape the caller actually invokes — so it no longer drops
connectedServices, and the catalog entry partitions the probe cache by binding.

Effort and ultracode require evidence of support rather than trusting an
unrecognised model id. reasoningEffort is session-scoped and is not cleared when
the model changes, so an unknown id alone is not a reason to forward a carried
level. The selected model's reported tiers are resolved once when the mode is
built and travel on it as modelEffortLevels, so spawn-time resolution and
launch-option hashing see the same value and hashing stays a pure function of the
mode. The request is clamped to those tiers; with no tiers nothing is sent. A
discovered id that merely contains a curated alias uses its own reported tiers,
not the alias table. Curated models keep their static table, so Haiku still never
receives --effort or ultracode, and neither does a session with no model selected.

Claude stays on dynamicProbe: 'static-only'. Turning the app onto the dynamic
model path is a separate, user-visible change and lands on its own.

feat(claude-models)!: consume the dynamic Claude model list

Flip Claude to dynamicProbe: 'auto' so the app runs the preflight models probe
and consumes the sessionModelsV1 list the CLI already publishes.

The flip switches the app from the static row builder to the dynamic one, which
carried less per-model metadata: `extendedContextModelId` was dropped by the
persisted session-model schema, the preflight parse, the probe cache, and both
dynamic row builders. AgentInput gates the 1M-context toggle on that field, so
without this the toggle would disappear for Claude and a session already on
claude-sonnet-4-6[1m] would lose its model controls.

Carry the field through every hop, and restore it from the catalog in
mergeDynamicModelOptionWithCatalog so a curated model arriving through the
dynamic path keeps its extended-context variant even when the dynamic source has
no reason to know about it. A dynamic source that declares its own variant is
honored too. `extendedContextModelId` is the only ModelOption field the dynamic
path was missing; the rest (label, description, modelOptions) already flowed or
were backfilled from the catalog.

Still open, tracked separately and not user-blocking for the list itself:
- modelEffortLevels is resolved once against options.modelId, so switching model
  mid-session keeps the previous model's tiers;
- the first turn builds its mode before the catalog resolves, so the first spawn
  of a discovered-model session carries no tiers.

fix(ui-pickers): keep the keyboard while typing a custom model id (#236)

The custom-model editor committed on every keystroke. Each commit pushed the
value to the parent, which regenerated the picker option list with a fresh
detail-content closure and remounted the input, so the keyboard closed after

blur followed by unmount still commits once.

Correlate journal agents with imported sidechains and preserve provider-record timestamps across replay so resumed work is not presented as fresh.
Resolve unfinished agents from observed run completion, API termination, process death, and explicit stop while preserving honest start and completion evidence.
Wire the fail-closed transcript registrar through local and unified-terminal launchers and settle outstanding background tasks only after an observed orderly stop.

Classify ChatGPT-account model incompatibility as plan-invalid recovery evidence instead of an opaque provider failure.
Route source-tuple supersession through the canonical runtime-auth handler so stale reports are retired without probing or mutating the current binding.

fix(ui-agent-activity): qualify live work with session observation

Surface one session-level observation caveat while work is in flight instead
of rewriting individual agent statuses when the host can no longer observe the
session. Build the model from the canonical activity evidence index so normal
subagents and team-member-only activity follow the same truth rules.

staleness as the canonical motion owners. Preserve row separators and minimum
touch targets across disclosure and overflow layouts, with focused host-parity,
motion, and accessibility coverage.

fix(claude): preserve sidecar evidence before roster discovery

Memoize the complete best-known workflow-agent sidecar profile when transcript
evidence arrives before the journal introduces the agent. Apply its earliest
start, stable sidechain, model, title, and terminal API-error evidence through a
single owner once the roster entry appears, while preserving self-reported
outcomes over inferred cancellation.

feat(cli): preserve the predecessor plugins command contract

Register a compatibility-only `plugins` command that accepts the predecessor
`list --json` invocation and returns the versioned empty catalog expected by
older automation. Reject unsupported plugin operations explicitly and keep the
command from falling through to the default agent launcher.

fix(server): project revisions for legacy service credentials

Resolve every connected-service credential revision through the canonical
revision owner, including legacy rows whose metadata predates explicit fencing.
Select row identity in the profile query so clients receive deterministic
revision entries for active and backup credentials instead of silently omitting
unfenced materializations.

fix(daemon): fence session runners by process instance

Persist OS process-instance fingerprints alongside legacy command hashes in
runner locks and tracked-session state. Use fingerprint equality to prove the
same runner and inequality to prove PID reuse, while treating legacy records
without that evidence fail-closed instead of killing or replacing a live PID
because command classification drifted.

Propagate the identity contract through heartbeat recovery, marker reattach,
planned restart, serviceability repair, webhook registration, and explicit
stop. Preserve the disabled automatic-respawn policy while allowing observed
runner loss and intentional stop paths to retire state safely without signaling
an unrelated process.

fix(terminal-host): verify prompts around submit

Centralize pre-submit staging and post-submit clearance verification in the
prompt submission owner. Wait for the exact prompt to appear before sending
Enter, require two stable absence observations before declaring delivery, and
report whether a failed attempt could have reached the pane so callers can
avoid unsafe duplication.

Apply the contract to PTY, tmux, and Zellij adapters, including size-aware write
timeouts and one bounded Enter retry when the composer demonstrably remains
pending.

fix(ui-sessions): stop runners missing daemon tracking

Treat `tracked_runner_absent` as evidence that strict daemon bookkeeping cannot
serve the stop, then fall back to the session runner RPC under the same server
scope. Preserve the daemon result when the live runner route is unavailable so
the UI does not misreport an incomplete stop as successful or as a generic
upgrade problem.

perf(ui-popover): measure anchors before the first frame

Start the initial anchor measurement synchronously when a popover opens so its
otherwise invisible portal does not spend a guaranteed frame waiting to become
positionable. Keep frame-delayed retries for anchors whose layout genuinely has
not settled, and pin the first-measure contract with a native-host test that
withholds queued animation frames.

feat(ui-sessions): unify pane and screen resource navigation

Introduce one session-target resolver that opens files, commits, terminals,
agent rosters, and transcripts in desktop panes or dedicated phone routes based
on the active layout. Give every session surface the same canonical pane scope,
remove route-local redirection policy, and route header, activity, work-state,
and structured-reference entry points through that owner.

Add transcript details as a typed resource for imported workflow-agent
sidechains. Project sidechain records through the reducer's canonical message
converter, extract one shared hydration/transcript body from the tool view, and
render the result read-only without fabricating a tool call or subagent model.
Register native routes, preserve focus/history semantics, reject cross-session
resources, and localize the new transcript and agent navigation states.

test(ui-sessions): type route fallback assertions

Address invalid-link fallbacks through the standard test ID instead of
comparing React element types to host strings, and drive hook effects through
the current testkit signature. This preserves the route behavior assertions
while keeping the feature corridor valid under strict TypeScript.
fix(profiles): refresh MiniMax model id

fix(ui): hide signup and show a specific message when the server disables sign-ups

When a server disables every signup/provision method, the welcome panel
no longer renders a Create account button destined for 403; Login is
promoted to the primary CTA. authGetToken now parses the JSON error body
of a failed POST /v1/auth and throws a typed AuthTokenRequestError, and
the welcome screen maps signup-disabled to a specific translated message
(new errors.signupDisabled key in all locales).

Fixes #251

fix(ui): address review feedback on signup-disabled copy and spec

- ca: use the informal tu imperative to match the rest of the locale
- pt: match the welcome screen's Brazilian-leaning phrasing
