feat(issue-triage): separate evidence routing from diagnosis

Add dedicated read-only skills for multi-issue normalization and deep diagnosis,
including untrusted-input handling, private evidence capability checks,
version-aware dispositions, clustering, and explicit presentation ownership.
Route runtime diagnosis, GitHub operations, implementation, and independent
session delegation through their existing canonical owners.

Constrain GitHub workflows to sanitized context transport: remove automatic
coding-agent assignment, make the manual workflow read-only, upload its private
context artifact, and pin those boundaries with a wiring contract test.

feat(protocol): carry the first pending input through spawn

Define and export a strict versioned first-input payload for fresh-session
spawn. Preserve prompt and opaque local-id bytes, reject blank identities, and
allow structured message metadata so the runner can commit the first turn to
Pending without inventing a second delivery identity.

feat(protocol): type incomplete session control outcomes

Represent stopped-but-unconfirmed projection, incomplete cleanup, and physical
stop uncertainty as discriminated session-stop outcomes while continuing to
accept the released `{stopped:false}` shape. Extend execution-run transport
errors for unsupported protocols and unavailable targets, and preserve these
structured dependency results as successful action executions.

fix(protocol): classify Claude workflow starts as active

Treat Dynamic Workflow `start` and `started` status signals as active from the
moment an agent launches. This prevents short-lived agents from remaining
unknown for their entire visible lifetime before a progress event arrives.

fix(provider-install): size Codex extraction limits for releases

Allow provider runtime specifications to set bounded archive extraction limits
and propagate them through the shared GitHub-release installer. Raise Codex's
per-file and expanded ceilings to 384 MiB so checksum-pinned Windows releases
fit while retaining archive path, entry-count, compression-ratio, and total
expansion protections.

fix(server-pending): bound publisher materialization admission

Carry one absolute request deadline through socket handling, publisher-presence
serialization, lock admission, transaction acquisition, and queue
materialization. Remove expired lock waiters, bound transaction retries and body
execution, and roll back writes that outlive the request instead of allowing
late materialization after the caller has timed out.

Validate the publisher fence and rejoin claim inside the same transaction that
reads and consumes Pending. Preserve pending-count repair as a hint-based fast
path, map deadline failures explicitly, and publish session updates only after
the authoritative transaction completes.

fix(stack): create named environments exclusively

Refuse `stack new` when the name already exists and create the environment file
under its lock with exclusive filesystem semantics. This closes the check/write
race so concurrent creators cannot overwrite an existing stack configuration,
and directs intentional edits through the dedicated edit or env commands.

fix(stack): skip redundant daemon watch restarts

Compare the healthy daemon's dist-closure fingerprint and PID with the current
runtime state before activating a watch generation. Skip restart when the
candidate dist is already serving, while retaining generation and cold-start
checks when identity cannot be proven.

fix(stack): reset Expo restart budget after healthy runs

Record when a supervised Expo process becomes certified and reset its crash
attempt counter after a configurable sustained healthy interval. Preserve
bounded exponential restart behavior for rapid crash loops while allowing a
later isolated failure to recover instead of inheriting stale historical debt.

fix(cli-build): unify runtime import probe admission

Use one 120-second import budget for build finalization and stack integrity
checks so a source-built CLI accepted by one path is not rejected by another.
Exit the isolated import probe after successful module initialization, keeping
process-lifetime handles out of this linking check while preserving failures
for import errors and timeouts.

feat(cli-automation): make command output delivery reliable

Make JSON envelopes an awaited stdout write boundary so large responses are not
truncated when Node or Bun exits and broken pipes fail visibly. Migrate command
handlers to await that contract, keep JSON stdout free of diagnostics, and
extend the logger testkit to capture direct stream writes.

Centralize positional parsing so flags and their values cannot be mistaken for
session, run, or action identifiers. Complete nested session help coverage,
preserve structured action and stop outcomes, normalize automation errors and
exit codes, and apply the versioned envelope contract consistently across auth,
machine, MCP, profiles, relay, server, tools, and session commands.

fix(session-delivery): serialize Pending commits and acknowledgements

Route user-message delivery through one ordered commit queue, preserving the
opaque local identity across encrypted Pending transport and direct transcript
storage. Wait for committed turn-end drains, classify ambiguous RPC outcomes,
and prevent later sends or acknowledgements from overtaking an unsettled
message while retaining retry-safe delivery evidence.

fix(claude-terminal): arbitrate Pending injection truthfully

Give unified-terminal input one arbiter for startup, resumed hooks, Pending
blocks, and direct prompt injection. Preserve delivery ownership until staging
and submit verification settle, classify verification failures explicitly, and
prevent resumed hook activation or a competing writer from duplicating an
ambiguous prompt.

Simplify Claude's verification policy around the shared terminal-host contract
and propagate the failure reason consistently through PTY, tmux, Zellij, and
the provider-neutral injection result.

perf(ui-selection-list): stabilize measured step transitions

Separate body measurement from visible rendering so option identity changes do
not remount the measure host or duplicate row work. Reconcile root-step updates
without discarding active navigation state, derive measured body height through
one owner, and animate only between certified dimensions.

Pin mount and render economy, root resynchronization, step-stack behavior, and
height transition contracts across static and nested selection lists.

fix(ui-workflows): present only evidenced phase progress

Flatten workflow activity when declared phases contain no bound agents instead
of rendering empty phase sections and fabricating a final phase position. Use
the canonical transcript execution-run classifier for tool rendering so an
interrupted outer call continues to show its streaming sidechain unless a real
terminal outcome or unavailable host proves the run ended.

fix(ui-transcript): wait for measurable entry restoration

Keep anchored entry restoration in a wait state until the list has a measured
scrollable range, including unsettled under-filled content and nearest-survivor
fallbacks. Do not open or close the entry transaction while waiting, so the
first-paint cover remains in place and the first valid geometry drives the one
authorized restore write instead of visibly flashing offset zero.

perf(ui-session-list): preserve unchanged projection identities

Reconcile projected session-list rows against their previous node identities,
reusing unchanged headers, sessions, arrays, and per-server maps while replacing
only rows whose payload or placement changed. Carry cached row signatures
forward by object identity so a one-session push no longer re-signs every row,
and keep visible-list selectors stable when unrelated server data changes.

feat(ui-spawn): transfer first input to compatible daemons

Gate pending-first-input payloads on the daemon version that consumes them,
then carry the exact text and stable local identity through both voice spawn
entry points. Keep older daemons on the post-spawn follow-up path so mixed
versions do not silently drop the initial turn.

fix(ui-spawn): reconcile scoped completion uncertainty

Recognize server-scoped machine RPC timeouts as ambiguous completion and
resolve the accepted spawn nonce instead of issuing another spawn. Read the
daemon version from the selected server's machine inventory, and give legacy
post-spawn follow-ups a bounded hydration grace before enqueueing exactly once.

Keep first-turn fallback delivery on the durable enqueue action for modern
pending-input wires, and load the follow-up subject outside per-test timeout
budgets so cold transforms cannot masquerade as runtime hangs.

feat(ui-session-actions): expose resumable sessions in the header

Add Resume to the canonical session action registry and derive its visibility
from the existing provider-aware resume and fresh-spawn capability checks.
Route execution through the shared resume-request seam, while hiding the action
for active, read-only, or unsupported sessions.

fix(ui-agent-activity): quiet roster motion during surface arrival

Suppress layout transitions until a newly mounted roster has outlasted its
host surface positioning, while retaining genuine row entrance animation and
reusing stable motion builders across rows and renders. Let shared scroller
hosts publish their motion-quiet window so compact popovers defer migrations
during scrolling just like pane-owned lists.

fix(ui-agent-input): publish popover scroll quiet state

Connect the shared agent-input popover's actual scroll surface to a motion-quiet
window and publish it to nested content. Agent activity rosters rendered inside
the popover can now defer section migrations while the user is scrolling,
without each content owner drilling a scroller callback through its API.

fix(ui-models): canonicalize unique qualified model aliases

Resolve an unqualified persisted or freeform model id to a provider-qualified
advertised option only when that suffix match is unique. Preserve genuinely
custom and ambiguous ids, keep model-scoped controls attached after
canonicalization, and label extended-context variants by their explicit id
instead of inferring them from any non-exact match.

refactor(ui-timing): match RN interaction scheduling semantics

Model React Native 0.81 New Architecture interaction scheduling as the
microtask-backed stub it actually exposes, while keeping web on a cancellable
macrotask and retaining a narrow fallback only when the native boundary throws.
Remove the unreachable starvation timer and environment knob, and document the
explicit picker-dismiss delay as the native UI sequencing owner.

fix(ui-metro): exclude CLI runner snapshots from crawling

Block generated `.runner-snapshots` trees under the CLI workspace from Metro's
cross-workspace crawl so retained deployment payloads do not multiply Expo
watch and scan work. Keep CLI source and similarly named scratch directories
visible, with path coverage for POSIX and Windows separators.

fix(cli-runtime): preserve Pi provider failure diagnostics

Follow nested ACP submission causes to the Pi-owned failure carrier instead of
collapsing an authenticated provider rejection into a generic session error.
Validate and re-redact the provider code and sanitized preview at the primary
runtime issue boundary so live turn failures retain actionable, safe details.

fix(cli-session): retain pending first-input context on retry

Merge daemon-carried first-input metadata into the canonical UI/CLI source
fields when committing the turn through Pending. Clear the environment handoff
only after the durable enqueue succeeds, so a transient failure retries the
same text, local identity, model, and profile instead of dropping context.

perf(cli-favicon): canonicalize restricted paths asynchronously

Prepare restricted-root authorization once per favicon request, resolving each
root and target through asynchronous realpath while preserving missing
segments and Windows comparison semantics. Stop discovery at the first usable
candidate, avoid lower-priority source reads, and parse object icon declarations
independently of property order without blocking the daemon event loop.
fix(ui): render agent-style TeX math delimiters

feat(provider-install): publish declared Codex package runtimes

Select the canonical Codex package assets and declare the exact runtime files
Happier installs on each platform, excluding bundled metadata and unrelated
tools. Validate every required archive member before activation and preserve
the package directory layout needed by the code-mode host and Windows helpers.

Promote managed candidates through a same-filesystem backup so extraction,
validation, or rename failures leave the previous release active instead of
deleting a working installation.

fix(cli-pi): bind broker readiness to session lifecycle

Carry the runner cancellation signal through the ACP backend session-open
contract and opt Pi into that lifecycle. Bound broker handshake, state, create,
and resume work by one session-open deadline; cancel pending RPC requests
without leaking timers; and fail closed when the exact Pi child exits or its
extension never proves readiness.

Keep brokered processes stable across auth-file changes until a matching
durable session can be resumed, validate replacement session identity before
provider effect, and surface broker/provider failures through redacted,
structured ACP runtime diagnostics.

fix(stack-runtime): follow the active source-backed launch mode

Read the live stack runtime record before resolving nested CLI launch mode and
prefer its source-backed state over a snapshot requirement inherited from the
stack environment. Keep explicit --runtime and --source overrides authoritative,
and require the recorded owner process to still be alive so stale state cannot
weaken snapshot enforcement.

Cover source-backed active stacks, stale runtime records, snapshot provenance,
and wrapper flag stripping through resolver and launch integration tests.

fix(stack-build): rebuild the CLI after workspace dependency repair

Track whether stack dependency preparation rebuilt a workspace dependency and
feed that result into automatic CLI build selection. Force a full CLI rebuild
when repaired dependency output may have invalidated an otherwise fresh bundle,
while retaining the existing fast path for unchanged workspaces and service mode.

Exercise the behavior with a portable fake Yarn harness and verify that stale
workspace output is repaired before the CLI bundle is republished.

fix(ghops): verify bot identity before GitHub commands

Validate the resolved credential against GitHub's user endpoint before forwarding
ordinary gh commands, so issue and repository mutations cannot silently run as a
different account. Keep wrapper-level help token-free while forwarding nested
subcommand help to gh, and document the required issue write permission.

Cover wrong-account rejection, nested help, environment and Keychain credentials,
path expansion, forwarding, and token redaction in the wrapper test suite.

fix(cli-capabilities): probe selected connected-service auth

Declare which provider preflight adapters require materialized connected-service
credentials and prepare those credentials through the canonical spawn resolver
before probing models, modes, or config options. Pass the resulting environment
through provider command resolution and subprocess launch, isolate cached answers
by materialized selection, clean up one-shot materialization, and fail closed
instead of silently probing ambient auth.

Remove Codex's legacy stable-home shortcut, extend the same contract to OpenCode
and Pi, and cache conclusive Claude parser capabilities by installed binary
fingerprint without caching timeouts or launch failures.

feat(cli-diagnostics): report stalled serialized work queues

Add a failure-isolated observer for promise-tail queues that reports one slow
operation or cumulative queue wait per incident and one recovery event without
retaining payloads or logging normal traffic. This also supplies the helper
already consumed by the session commit queue in the existing delivery path.

Instrument Codex app-server bridge work with bounded operation metadata so a
stalled provider notification, request, finalization, or shutdown can be
identified without changing queue ordering, rejection recovery, or liveness.

fix(daemon-control): publish readiness and expose stalls

Keep the daemon offline until every required machine-control RPC registration is
acknowledged, then publish running even when acknowledgements arrive after the
initial deadline. Scope late acknowledgements to the current transport generation
and coalesce duplicate running-state publication.

Track only method names and durations for active RPC handlers, log bounded
event-loop stall context, and add request receive/completion timing to the local
control server. Start and stop the monitor with daemon lifecycle without exposing
request payloads or allowing diagnostic failures to affect control execution.

fix(daemon-delivery): report pending queue wake outcomes

Extract fire-and-forget pending-queue wake publication behind one owner that
distinguishes successful publication, runtime unavailability, transport failure,
and shutdown suppression. Emit safe operational outcomes by default while
retaining serialized failure details only at debug level.

Use the helper for attached-session wakeups without changing the guarded RPC,
session-identity check, or idempotent delivery contract.

fix(connected-services): require complete quota preflight

Propagate abort signals through account-mode, credential, group, and quota reads
so aggregate quota refresh can honor a bounded deadline. Return explicit complete
or incomplete probe evidence, settle contended and stalled reads on cancellation,
and retain completed-profile diagnostics without treating partial results as
selection authority.

Prevent auth-group switching and credential materialization from committing an
account chosen from incomplete quota evidence. Bound spawn preflight to the
canonical quota timeout and return a stable validation failure when hard-limit
availability cannot be verified, while preserving the authoritative current
profile for soft-threshold uncertainty.

fix(cli-claude): acknowledge bypass mode per launch

Build one private Claude settings overlay that combines generated hook settings
with launch-only safety acknowledgement for an explicitly selected
bypassPermissions mode. Keep the base settings immutable, prefer a mode-0600
sibling file, and fall back to safe inline JSON without exposing keys marked as
unsafe for argv.

Preserve resume and permission flag ordering, and make the Windows shim assertion
accept the canonical COMSPEC-resolved cmd.exe path.

fix(cli-claude): reconcile durable workflow agents

Read Claude's durable workflow run record beside the journal and feed its
workflow_progress facts through the canonical correlation path. Backfill labels,
phases, metrics, and concrete agent ids onto existing journal rows, adopting
provisional index identities instead of publishing duplicate agents.

At startup, merge workflow headlines with orphaned roster entries so interrupted
agents are resolved even when their run aged out or was already terminal. Preserve
authoritative terminal run status, retain agent-provided names, and avoid
inventing success for agents left running by a dead process.

fix(opencode): bind Windows server activation to listener

Expose one canonical cross-platform PID inspector from daemon diagnostics and use
it for OpenCode process identity. On Windows cmd-wrapper launches, resolve the
actual listening child through netstat and CIM ancestry without colliding with
PowerShell's read-only PID variable.

Bind broker activation proof to that listener generation and its nonempty command
hash so wrapper custody cannot be mistaken for provider custody. Keep POSIX
zombie detection, and make its tests inject platform semantics without mutating
global process state across concurrent test files.

fix(opencode): gate first prompt on required MCP readiness

Start OpenCode without blocking session initialization, but retain a shared
readiness outcome for the required Happier MCP server. Before accepting the first
prompt, wait for that registration and distinguish provider turn rejection from
a turn that already resolved while readiness was pending.

Reject missing commands, failed registration, and failed MCP status before
provider acceptance while allowing optional MCP servers to remain best-effort.

refactor(cli-spawn): reuse the pending input contract

Replace three hand-written pending-first-input validators with the protocol-owned
PendingFirstInputV1 schema at RPC compatibility parsing, machine dispatch, and
daemon environment serialization boundaries. Preserve the existing nonblank text
and local-id contract while preventing those readers from drifting independently.

fix(cli-runs): classify exhausted execution fallbacks

Recognize structured and legacy RPC method-unavailable failures separately from
transport target unavailability. Attempt bounded marker and transcript recovery
as before, but when it yields no run, return stable protocol-unsupported or
target-unavailable codes instead of a generic unknown error.

Preserve authoritative service not-found results and continue rethrowing errors
that are unsafe for compatibility fallback.

fix(cli-sessions): preserve pagination and stop outcomes

Expose the server page's hasNext bit alongside its cursor so CLI consumers can
distinguish an empty terminal page from an empty intermediate page.

Return protocol-owned stop outcomes when physical retirement, cleanup, or relay
projection remains unconfirmed. Distinguish proven host destruction with cleanup
failure from an unproven physical stop, and retain a plain successful result only
after both physical stop and inactive projection are observed.

refactor(provider-install): declare release assets in catalog

Move platform and architecture-specific managed release asset names into each
provider runtime specification. Let the generic GitHub release installer select
declared assets, retain fallback naming for future binary providers, and require
a digest before extraction for every provider.

Remove the Codex-only release parser now that it has no unique policy owner, keep
the explicit runtime-member allowlist and extraction limits, and document
OpenCode's managed installation support.

perf(ui-machine-picker): reuse capability rows and models

Subscribe capability glyphs to the narrow daemon CLI-detection projection instead
of whole machine heartbeat records, and salt cache entries by daemon state version
at that owner. Reuse one detection result across repeated rows and picker reopens
until the daemon version changes.

Keep machine selection option trees stable when only callback identities change,
while routing activation through the latest handlers and rebuilding when machine
data or favorite-toggle presence actually changes.

perf(ui-new-session): stabilize service selection trees

Keep connected-service and MCP selection step trees stable when popover hosts
replace render and activation callbacks. Invoke current handlers through stable
refs, preserve header accessory identity, and continue rebuilding options when
bindings, availability, reconnect support, or MCP selection data changes.

Memoize connected-service availability at its data owner so repeated popover
measurement passes no longer recreate every option and accessory.

fix(ui-spawn): hand the first turn to compatible daemons

For daemons that advertise pending-first-input support, expand a plain or template
first turn before spawn and include its stable local id, selected model, structured
input metadata, and connected-service profile in the spawn payload. Skip the
post-spawn UI send once daemon custody is established.

Retain the existing follow-up path for older daemons and session shapes that
cannot transfer the first turn, preserving mixed-version creation behavior.

fix(ui-sessions): restore archived sessions before resume

Detect an archived local session before issuing its resume spawn and unarchive it
through the owning server scope first. Fail the resume with a stable error when
restoration is rejected, clear the optimistic resuming marker, and avoid any
unarchive request for already-active sessions.

fix(ui-models): retain controls for qualified aliases

Resolve the selected model through the canonical effective-id matcher before
sanitizing model-scoped config overrides. This lets a unique unqualified custom
selection map to its provider-qualified option and preserves that option's
controls and canonical selected id.

Add focused picker coverage without removing the existing Grok model-control
contract from repository history.

test(ui-new-session): preserve worktree step on clock ticks

Assert that minute-driven worktree picker refreshes retain the same root step id,
so SelectionList updates stale timestamps without draining nested navigation or
discarding a worktree name being entered.

docs(github-ops): require exact mutation approval

Require every GitHub write batch to present its complete issue, label, comment,
assignment, project, and state payload for explicit human approval immediately
before execution. Re-read live targets, re-preview materially changed payloads,
and report applied results without inferring authority from broad triage requests.

Document bot identity revalidation, issue-write permission, opt-in roadmap
membership, and the canonical issue-diagnosis skill reference.

fix(ui-timing): type shared delays as void

Declare the shared delay helper as Promise<void> so retry and hydration owners can
consume it through their explicit sleep contracts without widening completion
values to unknown. Runtime scheduling behavior is unchanged.

chore(agent): add moving-worktree commit orchestration

Introduce a repository skill for reconnoitering, classifying, validating,
and grouping large dirty worktrees into coherent reviewable commits.

Document private-index and compare-and-swap transactions, partial-hunk
handling, concurrent-write preservation, index recovery, artifact and
oversized-blob exclusion, and human-understandable commit messages. Route
large commit campaigns to this workflow without affecting ordinary commits.

fix(cli-security): centralize Windows protected-path ACLs

Move Windows protected-file and directory ACL enforcement into cli-common so
all local-state writers share one current-user-and-SYSTEM-only policy.

Verify ownership, inheritance protection, reparse-point rejection, and exact
access rules after applying ACLs. Route CLI protected state and atomic MCP
configuration publication through that owner, including verification of an
existing destination before it is reused.

fix(cli-install): serialize managed provider promotion

Build each managed provider release in an isolated scratch candidate and
serialize only the final publication into the shared current directory.

Retire current releases under unique recovery names, restore them when
promotion fails, and defer cleanup when Windows keeps an old executable
locked. Preserve truthful install outcomes even when cleanup logging fails,
and cover concurrent, interrupted, and rollback promotion paths.

fix(cli-session): validate numeric command arguments

Parse session command integers as bounded safe values and reject malformed,
missing, or unsupported arguments before credentials or transports are read.

Apply consistent limits and defaults across session list, history, send, wait,
and execution-run list, stream, and wait surfaces. Preserve truthful JSON
errors at the top-level dispatcher and cover action-executor routing for each
command family.

fix(ui-composer): bound empty quoted suggestion tokens

Treat a quote after a composer suggestion trigger as an opening delimiter only
when a non-whitespace value follows it. This keeps quoted prose such as "@"
from holding the suggestion picker open across the rest of the line.

Preserve quoted tokens with real values and document the intentionally
unsupported leading-whitespace value shape with parser and formatter coverage.

feat(ui-composer): show provider logos for session mentions

Resolve each session suggestion's provider from its metadata flavor in the
session projection, preserving unknown providers as unresolved instead of
mislabeling them with a default agent.

Allow suggestion candidates to override their kind glyph and render the
provider logo with registry-owned optical scaling. Keep the generic session
icon as the fallback and cover per-row provider and unknown-agent behavior.

docs(agent): define documentation ownership workflow

Separate internal architecture documentation from the published user,
operator, self-hoster, and contributor site, and route each surface through
its package-specific owner.

Add an evidence-backed documentation skill covering release truth, canonical
page discovery, minimal editing, human voice, sensitive-data boundaries, and
risk-appropriate validation. Replace the generated docs-package README with
repository-specific commands and ownership guidance.

fix(stack-build): persist CLI input freshness provenance

Record the source-input freshness represented by each atomic CLI dist

fix(ui-appearance): apply Text Size and Content Width to the transcript on web

Two Settings -> Appearance defects in the session transcript:

- Text Size (uiFontScale) never applied to transcript markdown on web.
  Web Unistyles registers style values as non-enumerable, non-writable
  data properties; scaleTextStyle's clone kept those descriptors, the
  scaling assignment threw, and the fail-closed catch returned the
  original style. buildEnrichedMarkdownStyle then read the unscaled
  fontSize back off the raw object, pinning all markdown metrics at
  their 16px base regardless of the setting. scaleTextStyle now
  redefines numeric metrics on the clone (preserving enumerability so
  CSS-class-driven text rendering is untouched) and only fails closed
  for non-configurable metrics.

- Content Width (uiContentWidthMode) only applied after a reload.
  Transcript row caps read the static layout.maxWidth getter inside
  Unistyles stylesheets, which evaluate once at registration. The
  transcript row owners (MessageView, ToolCallsGroupRow,
  ToolCallsGroupUnitRowFrame, PendingMessagesTranscriptBlock) now apply
  the reactive useLayoutMaxWidth() value, matching the already-reactive
  ChatListInternal/ChatHeaderView/ItemGroup consumers.

Both proven RED->GREEN: scaleTextStyle and buildEnrichedMarkdownStyle
against the exact web-Unistyles property shape, and a content-width
component test verified failing on HEAD before the fix.

feat(pi): stream live context telemetry for the context-size badge

Pi sessions now get the same live context-size badge as Claude and
OpenCode. The bridge extension, when session-bound, listens for
assistant message_end events and writes pi's ctx.getContextUsage()
(tokens + contextWindow) as a single-line JSON marker
(happy-pi-token-count) to the Pi child's stderr -- an existing
machine-readable side channel (usage-limit markers already ride it)
that cannot pollute the LLM context.

PiRpcBackend.handleStderrLine consumes the marker before the normal
diagnostics path (no terminal-output noise) and stores the latest
telemetry. The existing per-turn publishUsageStatsBestEffort emission
(cumulative get_session_stats) now merges it into the token_count
tokens map as context_used_tokens / context_window_tokens -- exactly
the keys the UI token-count usage extraction reads -- and extends its
dedupe key with the context values so a changed live context
republishes even when the assistant-message counter has not advanced
(compaction, retries). Telemetry rides the session binding only,
independent of the tool disable flags; emission is skipped when pi
reports no token estimate (e.g. right after compaction), where the
existing compaction events already reset the badge.

Extension source version bumped to 2 so deployed assets refresh.

content + node --check), plus live pi runs proving one marker per
assistant message when bound and zero markers when unbound.

feat(pi): publish context telemetry at each assistant message, not just turn end

The context-size badge previously refreshed only when a turn went idle,
so during long tool-call chains the display sat stale through every slow
tool execution even though the model's context was already known the
moment the tool-carrying assistant message settled.

Publish now also fires at each assistant message_end — right before the
requested tool calls start running — so a slow tool call executes with
the fresh context size already on display. Telemetry prefers pi's own
get_session_stats contextUsage (the same live estimate pi uses for its
compaction footer, documented as current even mid-turn); the bridge
extension's stderr marker remains as the fallback for pi builds without
stats.contextUsage. Publishes are serialized through a promise chain so
overlapping triggers (message_end + agent_end) cannot double-emit, and
the existing dedupe key still suppresses repeats. The mid-turn trigger
is gated on bridge telemetry being present so plain embedders see no
extra mid-turn RPC traffic.

Extract Git-owned repository stack identity so names survive versioned checkout
moves, and keep repo-local database environment projection aligned with the
canonical provider transition.

feat(server): package migration support with every binary

Move database build-provider parsing into cli-common and consume it from server
client generation after shared dependencies are built.

Bundle the migration executable, schemas, migrations, schema engine, and selected
provider clients for both full and light server artifacts so deployment can use
one artifact-owned migration contract.

fix(relay): migrate databases during runtime installation

Resolve migrations from the installed server payload and run them after
promotion but before service activation, for local and delegated installs.

Preserve operator-owned provider, database, and file-backend settings across
updates, keep ordinary SQLite startup migration intact, and remove the duplicate
pre-install remote migration path.

feat(release): support reasoned validation refinements

Replace the legacy matrix of suite booleans with one risk-selected validation
profile plus explicit include and waivable-suite refinements.

Allow maintainers to waive exact-SHA CI or selected non-critical evidence only
with a recorded bounded reason, keep integrity-critical suites non-waivable,
remove release-time version bumps, and prevent issue-stage bookkeeping from
blocking an otherwise valid release.

refactor(server): separate runtime presets from database providers

Let full and light entrypoints honor an explicit server preset independently of
Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, or PGlite selection.

Centralize PGlite migration sessions, extend packaged migrations to PGlite, and
make the deployment entrypoint choose one provider-owned migration path before
server startup while respecting migration opt-out.

refactor(stack): centralize server preset and provider policy

Replace light-specific environment helpers with canonical preset defaults,
provider transitions, Prisma client resolution, and migration dispatch that
support every database under either server preset.

Keep managed infrastructure conditional on actual database authority, preserve
compatible external URLs, and route auth copy and migration flows through the
same provider owners.

refactor(stack): launch server runtimes by preset and provider

Apply canonical preset defaults and provider projection across source, runtime,
self-host, watch, and background stack startup.

Derive packaged or in-process migration launch from the admitted provider,
complete migration before normal server spawn, and preserve runtime identity,
restart topology, embedded directories, and compatibility with legacy light
packages.

fix(docker): run packaged migrations before server startup

Start artifact-based server images through the canonical entrypoint so Postgres,
MySQL, and PGlite migrations run before the server while SQLite retains its
in-process startup migration.

Document preset-independent providers, verify completed Prisma migrations in
release smoke flows, prune unused MySQL migration inputs, and exclude local
agent, native, cache, and QA artifacts from Docker build contexts.

fix(stack): bootstrap remote workspace owners before import

Install remote workspace dependencies without lifecycle scripts when cli-common
owners are not yet built, then build the required owner before importing stack
dependency logic.

Reuse the canonical dependency-refresh lock and isolated package caches so first
startup is ordered, repeatable, and safe under concurrent remote bootstrap.
Merge branch 'dev' of https://github.com/happier-dev/happier into dev
fix(release): align final dispatch contracts
fix(ci): preserve and accelerate full collectors

feat(handoff): add optional targetPath to handoff flow

Allow selecting and propagating an explicit target directory for session handoff. This change adds an optional targetPath field across the stack: UI picker (state, path browser lazy-load, and item to choose directory), openSessionHandoffPicker result type, sync domain flows (picker -> execute -> run flows), default action executor and delegated handoff, RPC handler payload, protocol action specs and session handoff schemas, and orchestration coordinator (prefers explicit targetPath over derived path). Tests were added/updated to cover selection, lazy-loading, and propagation.
fix(ci): stabilize runtime and end-to-end validation
fix(ci): stabilize collected runtime failures
fix(ci): complete rollback projection stabilization
fix(ui): reconcile stale rollback turn details
fix(ui): refresh rollback actions for committed turns

feat(self-host): gate packaged migrations behind one opt-out contract

RUN_MIGRATIONS and HAPPIER_STACK_PRISMA_MIGRATE now feed a single
resolveServerMigrationsEnabled decision owned by cli-common, and
resolveSelfHostServerMigrationPlan returns null when migrations are opted
out, so managed relay installs and stack runtimes enforce the same
contract instead of each re-reading the environment.

The stack server launch spec derives an explicit disabled migration mode
from that decision and the migration runner skips it, and run-server.sh
mirrors the same opt-out for packaged container start-ups, where the
shell entrypoint cannot import the shared helper.

run-server.sh also treats an unreachable database (P1001 /
ECONNREFUSED) as a retry condition inside the existing migration attempt
budget instead of failing the container on the first connection-refused
error.

Covers the opt-out decision with a shared unit test and the retry path
with a run-server.sh integration test using a fail-once fake migration.

fix(self-host): install packaged server runtime as a bin/ closure

Introduce serverRuntimeArtifactLayout as the single owner of the packaged
server runtime shape: payload-root resolution, executable names, and the
relocation of generated clients, node_modules sidecars, prisma, and
runtime directories under bin/. Relay runtime installs now relocate the
staged payload through that owner instead of hand-rolling the same moves,
and self-host runtime staging copies the artifact once, asserts the
packaged closure up front, and promotes the prisma/runtime sidecars and
the migration binary alongside the server binary.

Self-host runtime updates also preserve operator-owned environment
configuration: the rendered env file is now merged with any existing env
instead of overwriting it, so database provider and connection settings
set by operators survive a runtime upgrade. Env text merging itself stays
owned by cli-common's selfHostServerEnv module.

Covered by the new artifact-layout unit tests, relay install sequence
tests, and a self-host env test asserting operator database
configuration is preserved across updates.

feat(providers): promote managed CLI installs through an active release

Managed provider CLI installs now keep versioned releases under
.releases/ and promote them by atomically replacing an active symlink on
POSIX, so every new launch resolves a complete release instead of a
directory mid-rename. The previous current/ -> previous-* swap remains
the Windows path and the fallback for first installs.

Command resolution prefers the active release when it exists and falls
back to current/, keeping existing runner snapshots working while new
POSIX promotions switch atomically. Retired versioned releases are
cleaned up after promotion using the existing best-effort install log.

Covered by promotion and resolution unit tests covering the versioned
release layout, atomic swap, cleanup, and active-first command
resolution.

feat(stack): place server, expo, and daemon services on dev targets

Dev-targets configuration gains a version 2 runtimePlacement policy that
decides where each stack service runs: server and expo may prefer a
remote target, and daemons may run locally and on a named target set.
Placement is resolved into per-target service plans after target
preflight and persists as authoritative: a configured remote server that
fails preflight is an error rather than a silent local fallback.

The supervisor gains remote expo servers (with deterministic remote port
selection and health probing), remote stack stop, and SSH forwarding
worker commands; remote_commands builds the remote server runtime
configuration, projecting only the semantic light-server environment
keys a remote light server can honor. Repo-local execution now forwards
the resolved stack identity to the execution-host controller so adapter
runs target the invoking stack.

Dev startup consumes the placement policy end to end: requested local
services are intersected with the plan, remote servers contribute their
public URLs through an explicit --server-public-url override, and mobile
reachability is resolved from the effective placement instead of assuming
a local LAN address.

Covered by new placement resolution tests, an end-to-end remote server
placement fixture, and extended config, supervisor, remote command,
connection, and mobile URL tests.

feat(stack): expose --preserve-daemon on stack stop

The stop lifecycle already understands daemon preservation, but the
stack stop command never forwarded it, so stopping a stack always tore
down the daemon. stack stop now accepts --preserve-daemon to keep the
daemon and its runtime processes alive while stopping everything else,
parsed through a shared option resolver so tests and callers see the
same contract, and the help text documents the flag.

Covered by a new stack stop option resolution test.

feat(stack): default tui dev to the mobile dev client

Bare `yarn tui` (and `tui dev` with no forwarded args) now runs the Expo
dev client for mobile by default: the TUI child args gain --mobile
unless the caller already chose --mobile/--with-mobile/--no-mobile, and
the repo-local launcher forwards the same default. Watch remains forced
as before, and explicit arguments still win.

Covered by the TUI mode argument tests.

fix(stack): detect dependency content changes regardless of mtimes

The dependency refresh marker now hashes input content through
machine-portable identity paths instead of trusting per-path size and
mtime metadata, so touching a manifest without changing its bytes no
longer triggers an install, and editing bytes while preserving mtimes no
longer misses one. Inputs are identified relative to their installation
or component root, keeping marker state comparable across checkouts, and
the refresh state version bumps to invalidate markers written by the old
scheme once.

Existing marker invalidation tests are updated to exercise content
changes directly, and the new unit tests cover the identity and
portability rules.

chore(release): raise server runtime candidate aggregate limit to 2 GiB

The packaged server runtime closure now ships prisma and runtime
sidecars under bin/, which pushes well-packaged candidates past the
previous 1.5 GiB aggregate budget; raise the inspection ceiling to
2 GiB to match. Size violations now report the actual aggregate, the
configured maximum, and the offending file so oversized candidates can
be triaged without rerunning the inspection.

Covered by the server runtime candidate inspection tests.

feat(daemon): run Linux daemon workloads in systemd user slices

Provisioning now installs happier.slice and a lower-priority
happier-jobs.slice (CPU/IO weight 50, no memory ceiling or OOM policy) in
the systemd user unit directory, and the daemon consumes them: when a
user bus is available, spawned CLI sessions launch inside a
systemd-run user scope in the jobs slice instead of relying on the
legacy runner-side cgroup migration, which is explicitly disabled for
those children since the scope now owns the process tree. The detached
daemon itself starts in a critical scope with a memory-low guarantee so
session work cannot starve it.

Slice readiness is verified through systemd properties before use, so
hosts without a user bus or without the units keep the existing cgroup
self-migration behavior unchanged.

Covered by governor unit tests, launch spec tests for both the scoped
and legacy paths, detached spawn tests, and an extended provision test
asserting the installed slice units and their weights.

feat(website): promote worktrees and handoff to primary feature sections

Worktrees and handoff move from the small feature grid to full alternating
sections: worktrees present per-session Git worktrees as the ordinary
parallel-work flow (creation, branch picking, reuse, or simply starting in
the current folder), and handoff presents machine-to-machine session moves
with the two transfer-capable agents named explicitly, since most agents
cannot transfer their own session state.

The handoff grid entry is removed rather than kept alongside the new card
to avoid stating the same claim twice with different qualifiers, and the
alternating layout gains span presets for both new sections. English copy
and the generated per-locale slices and overlay translations are
regenerated accordingly.

fix(cli): suppress Claude prompt suggestions in unified terminal sessions

Claude's dim prompt suggestions render composer-like text that is not
real input, so the unified terminal's draft guard either fires on a
placeholder or has to weaken genuine draft detection. The launcher now
disables suggestions at the process boundary via
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false instead of tuning the
detector around them.

The fake Claude fixture used by unified-terminal tests mirrors the real
TUI's composer behavior: the idle prompt renders on its own terminal row
without suggestion text, typed characters are echoed, and Escape clears
the current draft, which the unified injector relies on to recover only
its own verified leftover text.

Covered by the spawn environment tests, fixture helper tests, and the
unified terminal integration expectations that consume the fixture.

fix(cli): bind unified terminal startup message custody to the launch attempt

The unified terminal kept at most one in-flight startup message, but the
record was not scoped to the launch that created it: after a restart or
restore spawned a new terminal attempt, an undeliverable-input callback
from the old attempt could clear the new attempt's message or replay it
from a second owner.

Each launch attempt now carries its own attempt id; only a callback
matching the current attempt may settle the in-flight message, late
callbacks from settled attempts are ignored, and a message confirmed
returned by the provider is blocked once, at disposal of the owning
attempt, instead of being cleared early and re-delivered later.

Startup/readiness failures still retry through the existing restore path
without blocking the durable row.

Covered by the unified terminal launcher tests covering settled-attempt
callbacks and custody handoff across relaunches.

fix(codex): keep auth apply settlement off slow provider diagnostics

Applying connected-service auth now settles at the exact provider apply
plus durable auth-store boundary. The account and quota reads that
followed were useful observations but made the fan-out RPC wait on them,
so a slow provider diagnostic surfaced as a false hot-apply failure.
Those observations run off the apply path and fence their writes against
the exact applied runtime identity, and the live verification returned
to callers is built from the applied identity rather than the mutating
latest-identity cell.

The auth apply RPC itself gains a bounded 60s timeout so a hung provider
session cannot stall the materializer indefinitely.

Covered by the app-server runtime tests for deferred identity
observation and the connected-service auth selection tests.

fix(codex): resolve session turn start anchors without blocking turn start

A codex app-server turn previously waited inline for the committed user
message seq before building its start anchors, delaying turn start when
the message commit had not landed yet. The tracker now reads the
committed seq synchronously when available and schedules the wait as a
background resolution guarded by an active-turn generation counter: a
resolution that finishes after the turn moved on is discarded instead of
merging stale anchors into a newer turn, and repeated waits share one
in-flight resolution.

Covered by the turn tracker tests covering deferred anchor resolution
and generation invalidation.

test(codex): wait for subprocess lifecycle instead of fixed sleeps

The listCodexSessionCandidates tests asserted pid publication and
process exit with a fixed 150ms sleep, which flakes under load. They now
poll for the pid file to appear and for the process to disappear with
bounded condition waits, keeping the same lifecycle contract without
timing sensitivity.

No production behavior change.

fix(pi): recover rate limits and retain terminal failures in pending turns

Pi RPC backends now treat provider rate-limit failures as recoverable
like capacity failures, so an assistant error event that begins a
rate-limit recovery does not fail the turn outright. Failure events
without a readable detail but with an explicit terminal marker are no
longer dropped: a resumed session replaying a stale error right after
the next prompt is accepted retains only that terminal marker for
agent_end to decide the turn, while detail-only replays still cannot
fail a turn that has not started.

Pending turns record the provider failure diagnostic and runtime auth
classification for the events that do fail them, and overflow and
capacity recovery flows keep their existing behavior.

Covered by the pending turn lifecycle tests for rate-limit recovery,
terminal-only replays, and pre-start failure retention.

test(cli): assert MCP bridge progress-before-result ordering deterministically

The remote MCP stdio bridge integration test raced the remember tool
response against its progress event, so a fast server could resolve the
result before the progress assertion ran. The test server now gates the
tool result behind an explicit release, proving progress is emitted
while the call is still in flight, and the result text is asserted after
release. Teardown releases the gate so failure paths cannot hang.

No production behavior change.

fix(handoff): extend RPC and poll budgets for long-running transfers

Handoffs transfer multi-gigabyte workspaces, but the machine RPC and
poll budgets were sized for metadata calls: the UI's default machine RPC
timeout was 90s against a 5-minute cap and target prepare polls capped
at 10 minutes, so large transfers could time out mid-flight and surface
as failed handoffs. The runtime config defaults and ceilings now assume
hour-scale operations (30-minute machine RPCs, 2-minute polls, 2-hour
prepare polls, multi-day ceilings for explicit configuration), and the
target prepare and source start retry windows grow to 10 minutes to ride
out target restarts.

On the source side, the tracked handoff start gives the target-resume
machine call an explicit 5-minute timeout via a dedicated machine call
builder, so a slow target import cannot be cut off by the default RPC
budget either.

Covered by the machine call builder tests and the runtime config bounds
tests.

feat(handoff): stream live transfer progress through tracked operations

Handoff start now reports real transfer progress instead of a static
phase list. The provider bundle writer counts bytes as it appends file
slices and threads an onProgress callback through the export store and
the session handoff start handler, and the tracked start operation
forwards those reports as action-operation progress updates.

The coordinator projects target-side session handoff status checkpoints
(scan, plan, transfer, stage, apply, import, finalize) into progress
updates, rendering the workspace transfer as a determinate byte progress
bar with the current file path once the plan's total size is known.

The UI progress flow subscribes to the action operation for its own
request id through a shared subscribeActionOperationByRequest helper
(also reused by the terminal-operation observer) instead of matching
session-scoped progress events, and the progress modal renders the
operation's determinate progress and label alongside the checkpoint
timeline.

Covered by the progress projection tests, provider bundle progress
tests, UI flow subscription tests, and the progress modal determinate
state tests.

test(self-host): cover migration closure promotion beside the installed server

Extend the self-host runtime promotion tests to assert that the complete
migration closure — the migration binary, runtime runner, and prisma
migrations staged from the relocated bin/ payload — is promoted next to
the installed server binary, completing coverage for the packaged
bin/ closure install.

test(stack): pin attended TUI propagation on remote dev-target commands

Cover the attended flag end to end: the Windows and POSIX remote stack
commands export HAPPIER_STACK_TUI=1 when attended, and the supervisor
forwards that environment to the target worker so the attended TUI
readiness contract holds on remote servers.

No production behavior change.

test(stack): pin the mobile-capable tui dev default in the wrapper

Assert the repo-local wrapper emits `tui dev --mobile` for a bare `tui`
invocation, completing coverage for the mobile dev client default.

No production behavior change.

feat(ui): share one path picker and browse recent paths in handoff

The new-session path selection list becomes a reusable owner under
components/ui/pathPicker together with its favorite toggle and path
input behavior, and the sessions/new components become compatibility
re-exports so handoff, settings, voice, and session creation share one
implementation instead of forking the picker.

The handoff picker target-path step adopts the shared picker: it now
lists recent target paths per machine (resolved from recent machine
paths and the target's platform) alongside the favorites and in-folder
sections, and its cards clip edge-to-edge children to the rounded card
boundary via a new ItemGroup clipContent prop that keeps outer chrome
overflow-visible. The picker modal entry drops its hand-rolled lazy
wrapper in favor of the modal system's own lazy component support, and
the shared handoff test helpers mock the additional typography variants
the richer picker renders.

Covered by the ItemGroup surface chrome tests, the picker tests, and the
updated handoff picker entry tests.

refactor(stack): drop legacy prisma schema provider inference

With the repo-only runtime model, the light and full server flavors share
the monorepo checkout, and the effective database provider comes from the
resolved preset rather than from a per-component schema.prisma file.
assertServerPrismaProviderMatches therefore stops reading and inferring
the provider from preset schemas and always accepts, keeping only the
component directory mismatch guard, and the tests now pin that the
provider is not inferred from a preset schema.

fix(ui): recompute rollback eligibility from current transcript state

Rollback actions were frozen at a stale committed-message set: the
transcript store intentionally mutates its id array and message map in
place while a separate version subscription re-renders the root, so an
identity memo over those inputs never invalidated. The input signature
is now computed during render, and the memo also tracks the session's
latest turn id and rollback-eligible turn starts.

Trusted runtime turn-start sequences are only used when the detailed
turns projection is current — its latest turn id matches the session's —
otherwise eligibility falls back to the flattened projection, so a
partially updated projection can no longer vouch for stale anchors. The
stable session signature that gates shell rerenders now includes the
turn id, rollback-eligible turn starts, and session turns, and the chat
list's extra data carries the rollback actions so rows re-render when
eligibility changes.

Covered by rollback UI support tests for projection currency, root hook
tests for in-place transcript mutation, stable signature tests, and the
chat list rollback action tests.

fix(ui): keep the legend web viewport stable across teardown and refills

Two web-only viewport robustness fixes for the legend transcript list,
landed together because they extend the same vendored patch:

A keyed item hold is now the renderer's authoritative viewport intent on
web: the hold target's itemId becomes optional so callers can ask
whether any keyed anchor currently owns the viewport, and the exit
anchor capture treats a live keyed hold like a held-end transaction —
teardown geometry is not a new reader decision, so it persists neither
an offset nor a detach.

The vendored patch gains preserveReadyToRender so a transient empty
dataset snapshot does not reset the list's ready-to-render state and
re-cover already painted rows when the dataset refills, alongside its
total-size and item-size bookkeeping adjustments that keep measured
sizes stable across those refills.

Covered by the renderer adapter hold-query tests, the anchor capture
deferral test for keyed holds, and the legend web row visibility
integration test proving a painted dataset is never re-covered.

fix(ui): keep the newest machine presence when snapshots arrive late

Merging a machine list snapshot could regress presence: a delayed server
snapshot carrying an older active/activeAt overwrote a newer activity
update already applied from another source. Incoming machines now
preserve the newest observed presence across the current server list and
the stored record, and machine display projections apply the same
preservation, so a machine shown as active does not flip to inactive
because an old snapshot landed last.

Covered by a machines domain test where a late snapshot must not regress
a newer activity update.

fix(ui): stop metro from crawling transient generated directories

Generated directory swaps in workspace packages briefly expose
`.tmp.*` and `dist.__finalize_backup__.*` paths before they are removed;
Expo's metro watcher then crawls those transient trees and can resolve
half-written modules. Both path shapes join the resolver block list for
all platforms, while canonical source paths remain watched.

Covered by the metro config block list spec with POSIX and Windows
variants of both transient shapes.

fix(ui): derive chip picker focus state during render

The chip picker panel synchronized its focused option with the selected
option through a state-plus-effect pair, so selection changes applied a
frame late and could focus a stale option. Focus state is now derived
during render from the current selection and options, removing the
effect churn and the stale-focus window.

Covered by the chip picker panel tests for focus tracking across
selection changes.

fix(ui): apply refreshed session config overrides during render

The new-session agent authoring screen kept remembered config option
overrides in plain state, so a backend or engine change that refreshed
the initial overrides never reached the form until some other state
happened to reinitialize it. Overrides now carry their source alongside
the value and re-apply the refreshed initial value during render when
the source changes, keeping the visible options in sync with the
selected backend.

Covered by the authoring options state tests for override refresh.

test(ui-e2e): seed replay fork enablement and harden fork specs

The fork specs each hand-rolled the settings walk to enable session
replay forking; a shared ensureSessionReplayForkEnabled helper now turns
the setting on directly in account settings, and the specs drop the
fragile prompt-visibility-as-persistence handshake in favor of waiting
on the terminal turn marker before reloading.

The codex app-server fork/rollback spec waits on provider turn identity
and server rollback eligibility instead of a client turn id, selects the
user row by exact text so quoted prompts cannot shadow it, and the fake
codex app-server harness answers thread/fork so the scenario exercises
the forked-thread resume path end to end.

No production behavior change. Browser suites are not executed in this
environment.

test(ui-e2e): seed folder organization via import in the sidebar spec

The folders sidebar spec now seeds folder assignment through the session
organization import API instead of driving drag-and-drop feature
toggles, removing the flaky UI drag setup while still asserting the
sidebar renders the imported organization and folder assignment
end to end.

No production behavior change.

test(ui-e2e): seed bounded transcript pages for viewport invariants

The viewport invariants spec seeded 35 turns to guarantee messages
beyond the server default page cap; with the test-only UI tuning that
requests 12 messages on open and six per older page, eight turns now
leave real older pages for the user-triggered prepend scenario, cutting
suite runtime. The per-event web telemetry field-diagnostics audit is
removed along with its duplicated field plumbing — the invariant
assertions themselves remain the contract.

No production behavior change. Browser suites are not executed in this
environment.

test(ui): scope the handoff picker glob input past the search input

The shared path picker renders a search header text input, so the
workspace-transfer test's single-TextInput lookup matched two nodes and
failed. The glob input is now selected by its placeholder key, keeping
the assertions on the transfer controls intact.

No production behavior change.

feat(stack): make postgres a first-class light-preset provider

Postgres joins sqlite, pglite, and mysql as a light-preset database
provider. Provider parsing moves to a shared parseDbProvider/
requireDbProviderFromEnv owner in the server storage module, and all
migration entrypoints route through one provider-aware `migrate:deploy`
script (backed by a new migrate.deploy entrypoint that selects prisma
migrate deploy per provider) instead of per-provider yarn scripts:
stack migrate and auth flows, the packaged run-server.sh entrypoint,
which now prefers the packaged happier-server-migrate binary and drops
per-provider schema selection, and the schema-readiness probes.

Because the light preset runs against a managed database, postgres
requires an explicit postgres:// DATABASE_URL: the effective provider
transition rejects missing or non-postgres URLs with distinct reasons,
and setup, stack edit, server-flavor, and repo-local entrypoints surface
those reasons as actionable errors. The managed-postgres authority check
recognizes the canonical local instance when repairing audit state, and
the prisma client import resolves the generated client per provider.

Covered by the migrate deploy, light plan, storage provider, and
run-server.sh tests on the server side; effective provider transition,
flavor, audit, provider projection, infra, and startup tests on the
stack side; and the auth copy-from integration suite.

refactor(ui): derive tab bar sizing from content without platform clamps

resolveTabBarMetrics drops the per-platform minimum interactive target
(44 iOS / 48 Android), the tabMinHeight metric, and the platform
parameter: tab height now comes from icon size plus symmetric padding,
and icon sizes step up one level per preset (20/24/28). The tab bar,
cockpit tab bar, and new-session capsule consume the simplified metrics
and drop their minHeight styles and Platform plumbing; the new-session
capsule's hit area is bounded to avoid the neighbouring tab's expanded
press area.

Visual deltas are intentional: slightly larger icons, content-driven
heights instead of clamped minimums, and unchanged compact-vs-regular
width contrast. The metrics tests pin the new two-argument contract and
the removed platform-target expectations.

fix(pi): recover rate limits reported by the active model provider

Rate-limit recovery keyed off the connected-service runtime auth
classification, so a 429 from the active model provider without a
connected-service selection (for example a zai subscription) classified
as neither capacity nor rate limit and failed the turn. Recoverability
now recognizes the provider's rate-limit status text first, then the
capacity classification, then the generic recoverable detail pattern, so
the turn stays open for resumed activity regardless of which surface
reported the limit.

Covered by a pending turn lifecycle case for an unclassified provider's
rate limit followed by resumed activity.

feat(ui): refresh session drafts when a session becomes visible

Opening a session showed a stale composer until the draft sync happened
to run: onSessionVisible now materializes the existing session draft for
the visible session through the draft sync runtime, gated on the
captured server-account scope still being active across the runtime
ready and materialize steps so a scope switch cannot materialize a draft
into the wrong account.

useDraft gains an active option so consumers can drive draft adoption by
their own focus signal: SessionView passes its surface focus instead of
relying on route focus alone, keeping autosave and conflict handling on
the surface the user is actually looking at.

Covered by the draft sync runtime scope-gate tests and the useDraft
active-state tests.

feat(stack): reconcile stack server profiles through daemon start

A stack-owned runtime whose port or URL changes between starts left the
CLI's server profile pointing at stale endpoints, and a stable stack
profile id derived from the server URL could silently diverge from the
profile-scoped state the CLI actually holds. Stack daemon start now
reconciles this explicitly: when the CLI home already has settings and
an active server id, it invokes `happier server set --server-id <id>`
with the stack's internal and public URLs through a dedicated
profile-set argument builder, deferring server-selection follow-ups and
capturing failure diagnostics without blocking startup on the best
effort update.

The stable stack profile id is derived from the comparable server URL,
CLI settings are read to discover the active profile's current URLs,
and `server set --server-id` updates that one profile's endpoints in
place — skipping loopback public-URL inference and advertised-URL
probing that only make sense for new profiles — and, when asked,
migrates machine identities, token subscriptions, and changes cursors
from a matching legacy profile so server-scoped state follows the
reconciled id instead of being copied piecemeal.

Covered by the daemon start verification integration suite, which
captures the profile-set invocation and asserts the reconciled profile
id, endpoints, and migrated state end to end (20/20), plus the server
profile unit tests.

feat(stack): reconcile the stack server profile on direct happier launches

The `happier` launcher now performs the same stack-owned server profile
reconciliation as daemon start: when the CLI home has settings and an
active server id, it refreshes that profile's endpoints through
`server set --server-id` before launching, replacing the legacy
stable-scope-id derivation, and fails loudly when the refresh cannot be
applied so the CLI never launches under a profile whose server-scoped
state was not reconciled.

Daemon start keeps treating the profile refresh as best effort with
captured diagnostics — a failing `server set` no longer aborts startup —
and the `hstack happier` integration suite captures the invocation
against a stub CLI to pin the reconciled arguments end to end.

feat(stack): allow an explicit fallback for server dev-target placement

Server placement accepts a per-service fallback policy: the canonical
configuration keeps fallback "error" (a configured remote server that
fails preflight is an error), while an explicit "local" fallback opts a
stack into local service when the preferred target is unavailable.
Invalid fallback values are rejected per placement, and the config
tests cover the accepted combinations.

feat(stack): publish the remote Expo projection with the runtime declaration

When a dev-target placement runs Expo on a remote target with an
explicit HAPPIER_STACK_EXPO_DEV_PORT, dev now records that projection
(web/mobile ports, host, target) as part of the initial stack runtime
state instead of after startup, so service tunnels and the watchdog
observe the intended remote Expo topology from the first publication.

The dev CLI build ownership test pins that the projection is declared
before the runtime start boundary.

fix(stack): keep the TUI server alive when daemon startup fails

With keep-server-running enabled, a failed daemon startup no longer
tears down the TUI's server: the failure is logged with the daemon
error and the dev flow returns not-started so recovery can be retried,
instead of propagating the error and dropping the server the user is
looking at. Last-green startup keeps its existing behavior.

Covered by the daemon watch resilience tests.

fix(stack): sanitize daemon subprocess env keys from stack test runners

Stack test runners now deny the CLI subprocess daemon keys
(dist-closure fingerprint, dist entrypoint, runtime-backed flag, and
stack runtime state path) alongside the existing daemon lifecycle keys,
and the integration runner applies the same sanitized environment, so a
test cannot inherit the invoking shell's daemon launch state.

No production behavior change.

feat(stack): resolve the ghops bot token through the execution-host broker

On a managed Linux workspace, ghops can now read the bot token through
the active execution-host broker's `mac-host` target instead of
requiring a local macOS Keychain or an exported token: the stack's
dev-target configuration locates the Mac execution host, the broker
exposes only the fixed bot credential over a user-only Unix socket, and
the token never enters the guest environment or disk. Local Keychain
and HAPPIER_GITHUB_BOT_TOKEN resolution are unchanged and still take
priority.

The ghops skill documentation describes the broker path and its
failure modes, and the ghops tests cover the resolution order.

feat(release): audit and smoke-test Linux desktop artifacts in CI

Tauri Linux builds now verify artifact quality before publication. A
pinned upstream linuxdeploy (checksum-pinned in the install action)
honors LINUXDEPLOY_EXCLUDED_LIBRARIES so host Wayland graphics
libraries are no longer bundled into the AppImage, the build job runs a
new artifact audit that rejects host graphics libraries inside the
AppImage and the deb/rpm packages, and both an Xvfb X11 smoke launch
and a Weston Wayland smoke launch must reach the desktop startup-ready
signal — emitted by the Tauri shell as a typed event plus an optional
marker file — before artifacts are accepted.

Updater artifact collection and the Linux bundler environment carry the
corresponding package and exclusion plumbing.

Covered by the new artifact policy, package collection, and bundler
environment tests.

feat(ci): publish a lane summary and allow verified canonical-CI reuse

The push CI workflow gains a ci_summary job that aggregates every
lane's conclusion into one machine-readable result, and the nightly and
release workflows accept an optional ci_run_id so an already-completed
canonical push run for the exact source SHA can be verified and reused
instead of waiting on a hosted rerun. verify-existing-ci passes the
explicit run id through to the existing verification contract.

No local runtime behavior change.

feat(release): carry the release channel through release change analysis

release-analyze requires an explicit --channel (dev, preview, or
stable), records it in the v1 analysis document, and emits the public
API review fields the release contract now expects (human review,
SDK release approval, and public API comparisons default to empty and
false until a reviewer populates them). The help-spec orchestrator
usage and examples match the new contract.

Covered by the release change analysis tests.

docs(skills): add the CI stabilization skill and broker-aware ghops auth

happier-ci-stabilize is a new skill for driving failing CI or nightly
runs to an evidence-backed terminal result: bind exact run identity,
collect the whole reachable failure set with the included collector
script, cluster symptoms into originating owners, classify from
evidence, fix one coherent batch, validate once per widening boundary,
and recover nightlies through the cheapest safe rerun or
verified-candidate resume path.

The ghops skill documentation is updated for the same execution-host
broker credential path the ghops wrapper now implements.

fix(cli): wake pending materialization instead of waiting on lost retries

A retryable-transport materialization without a server-provided delay
could consume the only eligibility wake and then wait forever: the input
consumer now performs one authoritative pending-queue reconciliation and
falls back to bounded metadata-wait backoff, while the session client
publishes the canonical eligibility wake when a reconnect restores the
negotiated contract and when a durable-row materialization reports
retryable transport. Connection recovery remains the owner of
subsequent wakes, so no polling loop is introduced.

Covered by the input consumer and user-message send delivery tests.

fix(cli): let runtime activity snapshots clear stale background activity

The session mutation outbox preserved strict ordering behind a blocked
authoritative session-turn/transcript mutation, which also stranded
later runtime_activity_snapshot mutations and kept stale background
activity visible. Snapshots are an independent projection: ordering is
preserved for blocked turn/transcript mutations while a later snapshot
still flushes.

Covered by the session mutation outbox tests.

fix(cli): skip browser open on headless Linux and Bun builds without xdg-open

openBrowser now detects a headless Linux session (no DISPLAY,
Wayland, or WSL interop) and skips the browser open instead of spawning
a doomed opener, and Bun-compiled binaries — which cannot resolve the
`open` package's bundled xdg-open script — verify an xdg-open on PATH
before attempting the open, logging the skip reasons at debug level.

Covered by the openBrowser tests.

fix(codex): pass the session directory on thread start and resume

Codex app-server thread/new and thread/resume requests now carry the
session's cwd, so a resumed thread runs in the session's directory
instead of the daemon's process working directory.

Covered by the codex app-server runtime tests.

fix(ui): honor a newer thinking-stop activity after durable projections

A daemon activity-off event can arrive after a durable terminal
projection has already advanced the session's updatedAt, and the
ephemeral filter then dropped it as stale, leaving the session stuck on
thinking. A thinking-stop whose activity timestamp is at least the
session's current one is now applied even when it is not a
timestamp-only patch, restoring the authoritative working-to-online
transition.

Covered by the plaintext update-session socket tests.

refactor(ui): drop the agent input's deferred parent text sync

The agent input no longer defers large-text parent synchronization with
its own debounce policy; the composer value flows to the parent
directly, removing the deferred-sync state machine and its large-input
special casing ahead of the draft ownership changes.

Covered by the agent input history navigation tests.

fix(ui): give web chip picker rail options their full touch target

The chip picker's rail options rendered at a 36px visual size with the
native touch target resolved per platform, but web pressables received
no compensation and were hard to hit. Web rail options now add vertical
hit slop covering the difference between the interactive target size
and the visual size.

Covered by the chip picker option selector state marker tests.

fix(ui): hold the web viewport through explicit jumps and user takeover

Explicit transcript jumps on web now run under a takeover effect like
entry restore: user scroll intent during an active jump preempts the
jump through the lifecycle owner instead of fighting it, the jump host
tracks its active operation with an explicit release, and route jumps
settle through a single onRouteJumpSettled callback whether or not they
succeeded. The scroll observation host forwards takeover requests to
the lifecycle owner and the target window adapter honors the held
identity, so a user interrupting a jump keeps the viewport they chose.

Covered by the jump host identity stability and navigation landing
tests, the web user scroll intent tests, and the scroll observation
host tests. One identity stability test file cannot run in this
environment (shared RN shim createRequire failure, reproduced in
isolation); its corridor is covered by the sibling suites.
