feat(handoff): stream provider-bundle progress from both transfer transports

The handoff prepare phase now reports real byte progress for the
provider bundle itself: direct-peer and server-routed file transfers
forward received-byte progress, the tracked start wires it through the
transfer handles, and the prepare-pending status carries an
import-session checkpoint with planned/transferred byte counts while
the bundle streams into the target. The coordinator projects those
counts into determinate progress updates and the progress modal shows
the packaging step's progress bar before workspace preparation begins,
with the UI flow passing the phase detail through.

Covered by the transport progress tests, the handoff RPC handler and
coordinator tests, and the progress modal determinate packaging tests.

fix(ui): retry draft hydration with scope readiness and merge defaults semantically

Draft materialization moved from the one-shot session-visible
notification into the composer: useDraft re-materializes the existing
session draft whenever its surface is active and the account scope is
ready, so a warm session that rendered before its scope resolved still
hydrates, and sync exposes the materialization through a scope-guarded
method instead of a fire-and-forget visibility hook.

The draft repository's merge now treats a missing field equal to an
intrinsic default (empty composer text, empty arrays, null routing) as
semantically equal, so a remote delete of a defaulted field no longer
fights the local document, and unresolved route owners defer message
fetches instead of publishing an empty loaded transcript while a
deep-link session row is still being applied.

Covered by the useDraft, session draft repository, and server-scope
fetch tests.

fix(cli): classify group-generation recipient applies by switch reason

fix(cli): re-establish stale Codex runtimes before local usage-limit recovery falls back

When an active Codex session's live usage-limit control path is stale or

fix(cli): tolerate denied rescue-mode priority normalization on Linux

A rescue session can inherit a lower priority from its parent, and an

feat(cli-acp): enable vendor resume for configured ACP backends advertising session/load

Configured (user-defined) ACP backends never persisted their ACP session
id: createConfiguredAcpRuntime hardcoded runtime-only session identity and
the customAcp manifest entry declared vendorResume unsupported. Stopping a
session and continuing it therefore always spawned a fresh vendor session
and silently lost the agent-side conversation, even when the adapter fully
implements session/load (e.g. agy-acp, which persists conversation
bindings and declares loadSession: true).

Adapters vary in session/load support, so publication is gated on the
runtime-declared capability instead of a blanket manifest claim:

- AcpBackend captures agentCapabilities from the initialize response and
  exposes supportsSessionLoad().
- createConfiguredAcpRuntime publishes the bound ACP session id to the
  customAcpSessionId metadata field (the field the UI already labels for
  configured ACP sessions) only when the adapter advertised loadSession.
- The customAcp manifest entry declares vendorResume experimental with
  experimentalResumePolicy runtime_checked: resume stays unavailable for
  sessions whose adapter never published an id, matching the existing
  Cursor/Grok pattern, and load failures surface at runtime.
- vendorResumePolicy and the two catalog runtime guards are widened to
  VendorResumeSupportLevel so the 'unsupported' guard keeps holding for
  future agents now that every declared agent is supported/experimental.

refactor(runtime): align embedded server database ownership

Route light-server and self-host database selection, migrations, artifact layout, and service environment through provider-aware runtime helpers. Remove duplicate SQLite and retry paths while preserving packaged and source startup behavior.

fix(stack): make Expo and remote supervision load-safe

Give stack-managed Expo processes a shared temporary-directory contract and keep remote supervision bounded under concurrent development workloads. Preserve explicit stack ownership and forwarded environment across local and remote targets.

fix(features): make server capability probing fail closed

Centralize server feature retrieval and decision inputs so missing, stale, or malformed capability responses remain unavailable. Add bounded caching and tests for runtime refresh, server scope changes, and feature-gate payload compatibility.

fix(rpc): bound request and readiness failures

Apply explicit deadlines to socket forwarding, HTTP writes, loopback readiness, and machine fallbacks so unavailable endpoints settle instead of hanging callers. Preserve encryption and plaintext compatibility while returning actionable timeout results.

feat(connected-services): enforce account quota selection policy

Add canonical quota-limit selection to connected-service group policy and carry runtime revisions through storage, switching, and recovery. Expose the policy in pool settings and cover mixed-version normalization, provider quota mapping, and candidate selection.

feat(devin): add catalog-defined agent support

Register Devin as a first-class catalog-defined agent across shared manifests, CLI execution-run construction, and UI provider composition. Add model, session-mode, settings, logo, and backend-factory coverage so Devin follows the same canonical catalog path as existing agents.

refactor(acp): derive runtime behavior from the agent catalog

Move ACP authentication, executable invocation, model discovery, session modes, and startup behavior behind catalog-owned definitions. Update provider registries and capability documentation so generic runtime code no longer carries provider-specific defaults.

fix(claude): preserve unified terminal lifecycle ownership

Keep Claude unified-terminal launch, input arbitration, prompt injection, transcript bridging, and liveness decisions under one session lifecycle. Cover late events, blocked input, startup timing, and terminal completion without duplicate turn state.

fix(codex): make app-server recovery deterministic

Bound Codex app-server RPC work, retain session control metadata, and reconcile resume candidates without replaying stale state. Strengthen runtime tests for interruption, recovery, and exact session selection.

fix(opencode): bound managed server lifecycle waits

Centralize OpenCode startup, lock, SSE idle, control-poll, and shutdown timing so failed managed servers settle predictably. Keep all timeout policy in the provider-owned runtime and cover stale lock and stream behavior.

fix(pi): preserve bounded provider failure diagnostics

Harden Pi RPC process startup, introspection, prompt failure, and thinking-level handling. Preserve only allowlisted retry and provider context in diagnostics while ensuring failed commands and child processes reach a terminal result.

fix(execution-runs): unify control and completion semantics

Route execution-run creation, model options, permissions, steering, waiting, cancellation, and completion through the canonical run manager and RPC handlers. Remove duplicate timing decisions and cover exact inactive-session resume and terminal-host isolation.

fix(delivery): preserve pending composer intent across retries

Create pending queue requests through one owner and retain composer edits and attachments while inactive sessions resume. Align session-client transport and activation banners so retries do not duplicate or lose user intent.

feat(inbox): consolidate actionable session attention

Build the inbox from one content model combining approvals, reviews, unread sessions, and friend requests. Add stable row identity, mark-all-read controls, contextual presentation, and accessible localized behavior without duplicate selector ownership.

fix(actions): preserve operation reentry and acknowledgment state

Centralize action-operation selectors and reentry decisions so presented work remains discoverable without repeated acknowledgment. Update the inbox ledger and detail opening behavior around the canonical operation store.

feat(transcript): render execution completion and fork context

Project structured execution-run completion records and fork boundaries through the transcript registry and turn grouping owners. Preserve paging and empty-transcript behavior while keeping derived items stable across refreshes.

fix(files): preserve detail tabs and diff scroll position

Keep file and diff details mounted through source-control refreshes and retain Pierre diff anchors without competing scroll restoration. Add regression coverage for read-only diffs, tab continuity, and refreshed file state.

fix(ui): stabilize navigation and accessible list controls

Refine desktop sidebar composition, prompt settings layout, and shared list, button, card, icon, selection, and modal primitives. Preserve mounted navigation state while exposing correct disclosure and focus semantics.

fix(sync): target refresh work without dropping local state

Bound background synchronization and target stale-session refetches while preserving account recovery, automation, pet, friend, artifact, and session state. Reconcile server updates through domain owners instead of replacing unaffected local containers.

docs(product): describe current session and compatibility behavior

Refresh generated feature references and document connected services, pending delivery, and compatibility behavior against the current implementation. Keep availability and ownership explicit for users and operators.

docs(issues): attribute transported comments to their authorizer

Replace the ambiguous trailing cc line with an explicit “Posted on behalf of”
attribution for agent-authored issue comments. Keep the ordinary authenticated
GitHub user as the human authority while clearly distinguishing the separate
account used only to transport authorized writes.

Update GitHub operations, diagnosis contracts, examples, and triage guidance so
exact previews and standing-authority comments apply the same wording.

fix(release): retain versioned rolling assets

Keep immutable versioned payload names alongside stable aliases so released
updaters and installers can continue resolving their signed asset identities.

fix(connectivity): preserve reconnect ownership across repeated starts

produced them. Late authentication and reachability results from an older
transport are ignored instead of taking a newer healthy connection offline.

Apply the same scoped reporting contract to connection and endpoint supervisors,
and cover scheduled reconnects, in-flight probes, and stale external reports.

feat(cli): add cancellable multi-select terminal prompts

Extend the shared animated prompt owner with Space-driven toggles and a
multi-selection flow that works with arrow keys or comma-separated fallback
input. Explicit Skip choices remain distinct from an exhausted invalid answer.

Settle Ctrl-C and close events through one cleanup path so timers and readline
listeners cannot leak after cancellation. Cover keyboard selection, plain
terminal input, retry exhaustion, and abort cleanup.

refactor(cli): share the numeric planet renderer

Extract the numeric planet frame into a dependency-light cli-common export so
setup and other terminal surfaces can render the same spherical texture without
duplicating animation geometry or ANSI concerns.

Keep color application in the terminal presentation layer, refine the welcome
copy contrast and available-height calculation, and verify the frame remains
rounded, varied, and bounded at supported widths.

fix(stack): preserve Expo export worker overrides

Carry HAPPIER_STACK_EXPO_EXPORT_MAX_WORKERS through stack environment scrubbing
so explicitly bounded Expo exports retain their requested concurrency when
launched through hstack wrappers.

Extend the sanitization contract to prove the override survives while unrelated
environment values remain governed by the existing allowlist.

fix(ui): keep horizontal row layout on the scroll container

Apply row spacing and alignment directly to the native ScrollView content
container instead of wrapping interactive children in an extra View. This keeps
option elements as direct scroll children and avoids platform-specific sizing
and gesture behavior introduced by the wrapper.

Retain the content test identifier as a non-interactive marker and cover the
resulting native tree and style ownership.

fix(cli): distinguish daemon startup locks from active conflicts

Treat a lock-only daemon inspection as startup evidence rather than an active
owner conflict until persisted daemon state identifies the running lifecycle.
This lets the expected daemon finish initial authentication while established
state-backed owners continue to enforce version, channel, and scope conflicts.

Replace mocked process assumptions with live lock-bearing child-process coverage
for startup and cross-endpoint ownership decisions.

fix(pi): preserve native tools in automatic permission mode

Translate the shared permission aliases before building Pi arguments and reserve
Pi's --tools allowlist for Plan and Read-only sessions. Auto, Default, and YOLO
now leave the provider's native, extension, shell, and custom tool catalog intact
instead of silently removing capabilities that Pi itself governs.

Keep unknown values fail-closed, document that Auto is not a workspace sandbox,
and align provider and low-level capability guidance with the tested behavior.

fix(pi): separate prompt admission from provider diagnostics

Treat Pi's exact prompt RPC response as the authority for admission while command
discovery and delayed provider events remain independent observations. Hanging
introspection can no longer delay an accepted slash-command turn, and stale or
uncorrelated events cannot reverse a negative response.

Keep failure-boundary tracing opt-in and sanitized while preserving useful
classified terminal diagnostics for the daemon. Extend lifecycle coverage for
busy turns, delayed commands, compaction, failure ordering, and redaction.

fix(gemini): keep prompt contents out of routine diagnostics

Stop logging prompt previews during normal Gemini dispatch and replace retry
messages derived from provider errors with bounded structured metadata. Operators
can still see the failed attempt, next attempt, retry budget, and classified
failure kind without exposing prompts, credentials, or provider response text.

Remove the obsolete preview formatter and verify both initial dispatch and retry
logging remain content-free.

fix(claude): match every permission request hook

Use Claude's explicit wildcard matcher for PermissionRequest hooks in both the
Agent SDK and generated plugin configurations. Empty matchers are not a reliable
match-all contract, which could bypass Happier's permission bridge for otherwise
valid provider tools.

Keep both Claude integration paths aligned and assert the serialized hook shape
that is handed to the provider.

fix(claude): preserve the user's default permission setting

Pass the Claude Agent SDK's runtime null sentinel when Happier resolves to the
Default permission intent. The SDK otherwise turns an absent value into an
explicit `--permission-mode default` argument, overriding the user's configured
`permissions.defaultMode` despite loading their settings files.

Continue forwarding every explicit non-default mode and document the external
SDK boundary behavior in focused option coverage.

fix(codex): keep authoritative app-server operations alive

Classify Codex app-server methods by lifecycle semantics instead of applying the
startup timeout uniformly. Resume and thread-start requests may have created or
adopted provider state, so they remain active until explicit cancellation rather
than timing out into an ambiguous duplicate attempt.

Retain bounded defaults for observational requests and cover both long-lived and
request-specific timeout behavior at the client boundary.

fix(codex): isolate app-server startup from user MCP servers

Build explicit Codex app-server configuration overrides that can disable MCP
servers inherited from the user's config while retaining Happier-managed tools.
This keeps startup lightweight and prevents unrelated user server failures from
blocking Happier's provider connection.

Serialize the disablement through the existing repeated configuration-argument
owner and cover empty, named, and pre-existing override combinations.

feat(installer): hand fresh interactive installs to guided setup

After a verified binary install, launch `happier setup` only when the machine is
interactive and still needs registration. Piped installers pass the controlling
terminal through to setup, while `--yes`, headless updates, and already configured
machines remain non-interactive and preserve existing service state.

Unify shell and PowerShell presentation around truthful install phases, shared
numeric-planet artwork, explicit motion controls, and actionable next steps.
Keep daemon installation opt-in for unattended runs and retain legacy CLI/service
compatibility checks.

Regenerate every stable, preview, and development website installer from the
canonical scripts and strengthen sync, handoff, daemon-default, and presentation
contracts across Unix and Windows.

feat(cli): make guided setup the canonical onboarding flow

Guide interactive users through authentication, machine registration, provider
selection, and background-service reconciliation in one resumable setup command.
Present provider choices as a multi-select flow, preserve explicit skips, and
avoid restarting services before setup owns the final desired state.

Keep non-interactive and already configured invocations deterministic, separate
planning from execution, and ensure authentication invoked by setup cannot race
its own daemon reconciliation.

Update onboarding, setup verification, and hstack guidance to describe the same
entry point and recovery behavior. Cover first run, partial configuration,
provider selection, authentication handoff, and daemon decisions.

fix(ui): preserve and explain new-session drafts

Keep locally known drafts when exact hydration cannot yet load their session
context, so reconnects and partial server availability do not silently discard
composer work. Delete drafts only after the user confirms the corresponding
session action succeeds.

Project pending, failed, and ready draft states through one presentation owner
and render clear status in the drafts section instead of treating every record as
immediately openable.

Cover repository hydration, hook continuity, status presentation, confirmed
deletion, and the end-to-end composer draft flow.

refactor(cli): centralize cross-platform state symlinks

Move absolute file and directory symlink creation into one filesystem owner that
selects Windows junction semantics and normalized absolute targets consistently.

Reuse it for connected-service home projections and shared-state links, retaining
the existing hard-link fallback where supported. This gives provider-specific
runtime projections the same tested platform behavior without duplicating path
or symlink-type decisions.

fix(devin): isolate session MCP configuration from user files

Materialize Happier and selected MCP servers in a protected process-scoped Devin
configuration instead of modifying the user's home or project files. Merge
user-level servers, reject project-level shadowing, normalize command paths, and
remove the temporary projection when the provider process exits.

Use the shared cross-platform symlink owner for inherited state and pass the
session working directory explicitly so project discovery is accurate. Cover
existing configuration, collisions, cleanup, permissions, and unavailable-link
fallback behavior.

fix(acp): leave provider tool-call lifetimes provider-owned

Stop synthesizing short client-side deadlines for healthy ACP tool calls from
Auggie, Copilot, Gemini, Kilo, Kimi, and OpenCode. Long investigations and
provider-native thinking work now remain active until the provider reports a
terminal state or the owning session lifecycle is cancelled.

Keep initialization and idle detection bounded independently, and add one
cross-provider contract proving neither explicit adapters nor a custom transport
without a timeout hook manufacture terminal tool results.

fix(connected-services): negotiate auth-group response fields without CORS headers

Move newer auth-group reader capabilities from custom request headers into typed
query negotiation. Browser clients no longer require additional CORS preflight
allowlisting, while older strict readers continue receiving the released response
shape unless they explicitly opt in.

Centralize URL construction in the protocol package and apply it consistently to
CLI, server, and UI list and mutation routes. Extend the quota response schema
with optional allowance metadata needed by negotiated readers, and cover legacy,
opted-in, body-less delete, and structured failure behavior.

feat(cli): enumerate every runnable provider executable

Add a canonical candidate resolver that preserves explicit overrides while
enumerating distinct PATH, known-location, and managed binaries in configured
source order. Callers that must characterize multiple installed versions can now
do so without reimplementing executable discovery or silently falling back from
an invalid override.

Teach the provider catalog that OpenCode's compatibility binary may be named
`opencode2` while keeping stable `opencode` preferred. Cover duplicate removal,
source ordering, multiple PATH entries, known locations, and override isolation.

feat(server): project session rollback eligibility centrally

Derive rollback eligibility from committed session-turn evidence in one server
owner and publish it with session updates, list rows, and turn mutation results.
Clients no longer need to infer whether a rollback target is safe from incomplete
transcript details or provider-specific state.

Keep the projection consistent across socket events and paginated session
snapshots, and cover boundary transitions when turns are written, completed, or
lack the required committed evidence.

docs(agents): include browser preflight in compatibility review

Require compatibility analysis for cross-origin request headers to verify the
actual predecessor relay OPTIONS contract, not only the new server allowlist.
Document safer negotiation choices and the separate response-header exposure
requirement so browser compatibility failures are caught before implementation.

feat(actions): make direct tool exposure policy explicit

Define each action's direct-versus-discoverable exposure per session-agent, MCP,
and CLI surface, with settings overrides resolved by the protocol owner. Preserve
a narrow default set for bootstrap and safe execution observation while keeping
other actions available through discovery.

Apply the policy consistently to built-in session tools and the Happier MCP
server, retain collision-safe tool-name resolution, and document how clients can
discover and invoke actions without requiring every action to become a direct
tool.

Update CLI usage and permission guidance to distinguish portable intent from the
provider-specific approval or sandbox policy that ultimately realizes it.

feat(protocol): publish rollback-eligible session turns

optional preserves compatibility with older producers while allowing current

fix(permissions): admit only safe first-party action transport

Use the canonical action-tool classifier when deciding which Happier MCP calls
can bypass a provider-owned permission prompt. Safe first-party actions remain
usable without duplicate approval surfaces, while unknown and custom MCP tools
continue through the provider's normal permission path.

Apply the same rule to direct MCP calls, dynamic action execution, and encoded
shell-bridge invocations, failing closed when bridge arguments cannot be parsed.

fix(connectivity): ignore stale request outcomes after reconnect

Capture the connection supervisor's report scope before starting each request and
attach it to the eventual outcome. A delayed authentication or reachability
failure from an older transport epoch can no longer replace the healthy state of
a newer connection.

Retain compatibility with supervisors that do not expose scoped reporting and
keep authentication-only outcomes from affecting general connection health.

fix(sessions): preserve reconnect ownership for queued commits

Let queued transcript and durable-mutation work activate a session supervisor only
while it is idle. Once supervision is active, repeated queue admissions no longer
call start and therefore cannot reset or bypass the supervisor's existing retry
schedule.

Route ACK waiters through the same activation helper and cover both initial
activation and repeated disconnected admissions.

fix(sessions): scope delayed health reports to their transport epoch

Capture the active supervisor report scope before transcript recovery,
compatibility convergence, registration, and restart observations begin. Delayed
authentication or retry results can no longer downgrade a replacement session
transport after reconnect.

Preserve the unscoped fallback for older supervisor implementations while using
strict epoch ownership whenever scoped reporting is available.

fix(transcript): preserve exact provider custody through settlement

Track cumulative streamed transcript snapshots per logical segment and serialize
required commits without dropping a terminal update behind an earlier in-flight
snapshot. Keep exact provider-acceptance custody authoritative while its durable
settlement is still active, even when a concurrent pending projection is absent
or archived.

Bridge keyed transcript streams through one writer, retain terminal snapshots
until required acknowledgment, and cover reconnect, replay, and pending-turn-end
drain behavior.

feat(protocol): centralize connected-service quota selection

Resolve provider-limit identity and apply a pool's selected-versus-all allowance
policy in the shared protocol owner. Consumers can project quota meters without
reimplementing provider-specific fallback rules, while account-level subscription
and reset facts remain outside the filter.

Cover explicit provider limit IDs, legacy meter identifiers, and all-meter policy
behavior.

feat(codex): preserve provider quota limit identities

Attach Codex's stable provider limit name to every mapped quota meter while

and fetcher boundaries.

Apply the policy in daemon quota decisions and settings projections, add searchable

Move connected-service group loading, refresh signaling, projection identity, and

Preserve loaded data during refresh failures, reset state when service identity

Thread setup-managed intent through login so guided setup remains the sole daemon
follow-up owner, while standalone authentication can report optional service

Document the agent-install step in guided setup, method-specific terminal

Keep the field optional for mixed-version readers and cover schema stripping at

Run Kimi through the shared catalog-defined ACP backend with native MCP, model,

docs(kimi): describe current Kimi Code migration

Document current installer and login commands, ACP capabilities, Windows shell

fix(ui): restore derived context gauge and move Codex's reported-only rule to its provider module

The composer hid the context gauge for every provider unless the usage
record carried an explicit `context_used_tokens`, which only the Codex
app-server runtime and Claude's SDK path emit. Claude local sessions, the
default mode, forward raw transcript usage rows and lost the gauge; the
"always show context size" setting stopped working as well.

The protocol's per-message usage record (input + cache tokens) is the
active context for every provider that fills it honestly, so the composer
derives the gauge from it again. Codex is the exception: its token rows are
cumulative thread totals kept as account usage snapshots under a stable
usage-report key, so its provider module now declares
`sessionUsage.contextUsageBadge: 'reportedOnly'` and the composer reads
that registry hook instead of a global gate. The store field is renamed to
`contextSizeIsReported` since a derived Claude value is exact too.

exits 1, and renders no TUI. The unified terminal read that as a generic
startup failure and relaunched with identical arguments, so a refusal that is
deterministic for those arguments burned the whole relaunch budget before the

Claude names these refusals itself, and its startup error enum is described as
"Why Claude Code refused to start, so a host can offer the fix instead of a
retry". Happier is that host, so classify the refusal and offer the fix.

machine-readable startupFailureReason and falls back to observed text only for
wording that has actually been seen, so a guessed pattern can never misclassify
an unrelated failure as deterministic. Only the refusal Claude documents as

fix(cli): honor server transfer policy in delegated session handoff

The daemon-side handoff coordinator chose its transport from the request
alone: direct_peer whenever the caller listed it, with the server-routed
fallback always disabled. The UI's delegated handoff always sends
['direct_peer', 'server_routed_stream'] without a negotiated strategy, so
on a server that disables machines.transfer.directPeer the coordinator
still published direct-peer endpoints and the target could never fall
back to the relay.

Read fresh server features before mutating the source and select the
route through the shared resolveMachineTransferRoute policy, the same one
the UI uses. The source publication and the target preparation receive
the same fallback permission. Handoff fails closed before touching the
source when the features are unavailable, handoff is disabled, or no
enabled transfer route exists.

fix(ui): release transcript row height after an in-row collapse

A row-local collapsible (tool-row inline details, thinking bodies) changes the
row's painted height without changing its height signature. The row shell kept
serving the expanded measurement as its `minHeight`, so after any list
re-render while the details were open, collapsing them left a blank gap below
the row.

Once a mounted row reports a row-local expand or collapse, its natural content
height is authoritative and no reservation is applied. Heights measured while a
local body is open are not recorded, because a remount resets that body to
collapsed. A collapse also drops the growth floor recorded while it was open.

fix(cli): pin tmux session env and restart stale service daemons on install (#427)

* fix(cli): pin daemon-decided env in tmux session windows

A tmux window only overrides the keys passed with `new-window -e`; the rest
comes from the tmux server's global env, captured from whichever daemon first
started the server. After a relay or channel change, a tmux-spawned runner
therefore resolved a stale HAPPIER_ACTIVE_SERVER_ID/URLs/channel, looked for
the daemon under the wrong servers/<id>/ and never reported ready.

Derive the tmux window env from the same buildSpawnChildProcessEnv used by
regular spawns and pin every daemon-decided key (runtime context, release
channel, daemon-only keys), using '' for absent keys since -e cannot unset.
Share one server selection across the regular, Windows-hosted and tmux paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): restart or reload the stale service daemon on install

`service install` returned early when the installed definition already
matched, so a service daemon started by another CLI kept running and the
ownership check then timed out (Linux). On macOS, install only kickstarted
the job it owned, which keeps launchd's previously loaded environment, so a
changed plist (e.g. the release channel) never took effect. On Windows,
install stopped the owning daemon and then returned early, leaving it stopped.

Pass restartRunningDaemon when the service daemon runs another CLI or was
stopped for the install, skip the early return in that case, and reload the
launchd job (bootout/bootstrap) instead of kickstarting it when the
definition changed, the runtime was replaced, or a restart is required.
